# innostes UI - Complete Documentation

Generated for AI assistants and offline reference.

---

## Accessibility Statement (https://innostes.com/ui/docs/accessibility)

WCAG 2.2 Level AA conformance, component guarantees, developer responsibilities, and assistive technology testing.

`@innostes/ui` is committed to delivering accessible software for all enterprise operators. Every component in the library is built and tested to conform to the **Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.2 Level AA** standard.

Whether an operator at Northwind Traders Pvt Ltd navigates via keyboard shortcuts, relies on screen readers (such as NVDA or VoiceOver), uses voice control, or enables high-contrast display modes, all workflows must remain fully functional and efficient.

## Conformance target

The design system targets **WCAG 2.2 Level AA** across all four principles:

1. **Perceivable**: Text and graphical elements satisfy minimum contrast ratios (≥ 4.5:1 for normal text, ≥ 3.0:1 for large text and UI components). Visual status is never communicated solely through colour.
2. **Operable**: All interactive elements are reachable and operable via standard keyboard sequences. Focus order matches reading order, focus indicators are clearly visible, and modal overlays trap focus securely without keyboard traps.
3. **Understandable**: Controls provide predictable state updates, clear textual error associations via `aria-describedby`, and consistent interaction patterns across forms and dialogs.
4. **Resilient**: Components rely on semantic HTML5 primitives and WAI-ARIA 1.2 specifications, ensuring compatibility across modern browsers and assistive technologies.

## What the library guarantees

When you use `@innostes/ui` primitives, the library automatically handles:

- **Focus trapping and restoration**: Dialogs, sheets, and alert modals trap keyboard focus within the container and restore focus to the triggering element upon dismissal.
- **Roving tabindex**: Multi-item composite widgets (such as `Tabs`, `RadioGroup`, `DropdownMenu`, `TreeView`, and `ToggleGroup`) manage `tabIndex={0}` and `tabIndex={-1}` automatically, enabling direct arrow-key navigation.
- **ARIA attributes and live regions**: Tooltips, progress bars, toasts, and alerts emit proper ARIA roles (`role="alert"`, `role="status"`, `aria-live="polite"`).
- **Verified token contrast**: Base design tokens in `theme.css` and `dark.css` are validated at build time to satisfy WCAG AA contrast minimums.
- **Motion reduction**: Animations automatically disable or simplify when the user enables `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`.

## What the application team must do

Accessibility is a shared responsibility between the library and the consuming application. Application developers must ensure:

| Developer responsibility | Correct implementation | Why it matters |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Labels for icon-only buttons** | `<Button size="icon" aria-label="Delete order PO-881">` | Screen readers cannot interpret SVG glyphs without accessible names |
| **Form error linkage** | Use `<Field>` and `<FieldError>` | Associates error text programmatically with inputs via `aria-describedby` |
| **Heading hierarchy** | Use logical `<h1>` to `<h6>` levels | Screen reader users browse pages by jumping across heading structures |
| **Colour redundancy** | Pair warning badges with an icon | Red-green colour-blind operators cannot rely solely on hue shifts |
| **Table column headers** | Provide `<th>` headers with `scope="col"` | Allows screen readers to announce column context when traversing cells |
| **Alternative text** | Provide descriptive `alt` text on images | Screen readers announce image context for visual assets |

## Testing methods

Our quality assurance pipeline tests accessibility through multiple layers of verification:

1. **Automated component audits**: Unit tests run `axe-core` assertions across component render states to detect missing ARIA attributes, orphan labels, or invalid roles before code merges.
2. **Deterministic contrast validation**: A build-time check (`landing:docs-check`) parses all theme tokens and calculates relative luminance to prevent contrast regressions.
3. **Automated browser crawl**: A Playwright crawler audits documentation pages and interactive showcases for focusability, keyboard loops, and landmark semantics.
4. **Manual assistive technology testing**: Regular manual testing verifies auditory announcements and keyboard flows.

## Assistive technology testing matrix

We test `@innostes/ui` against the following screen-reader and browser pairings:

| Screen reader | Operating system | Tested browsers | Conformance status |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **VoiceOver** | macOS (Sequoia / Sonoma) | Safari, Google Chrome | Fully verified in continuous QA |
| **NVDA** | Windows 11 | Mozilla Firefox, Google Chrome | Fully verified in continuous QA |
| **TalkBack** | Android 14 | Chrome Mobile | Verified for mobile ERP layouts |
| **JAWS** | Windows 11 | Edge, Chrome | Scheduled on enterprise roadmap |
| **Orca** | Linux (Ubuntu / Debian) | Firefox | Scheduled on enterprise roadmap |

## Known issues and continuous hardening

We maintain an active audit tracker (`AUDIT.md`) documenting accessibility improvements:

- **LIB-003**: Customisable internationalisation strings across all ERP widgets (`DataTable`, `TreeView`, `KanbanBoard`) to eliminate hardcoded English text.
- **LIB-004**: Token contrast adjustments across light and dark mode tokens to ensure 100% WCAG AA compliance across all semantic pairings.
- **LIB-007**: Migration from physical directional CSS classes to logical bidirectional properties (`inset-inline-start`, `margin-inline-end`) for full RTL language accessibility.

## Reporting an accessibility problem

If you discover an accessibility barrier or an unannounced state in any `@innostes/ui` component:

1. Open an issue on our repository describing the component, the expected vs actual behaviour, and the assistive technology used (including version numbers).
2. Or contact our accessibility working group directly at `accessibility@innostes.com`.
3. Critical accessibility defects affecting production applications are prioritised as S1 bugs in accordance with our governance policy.

---

## Cartesian Charts (https://innostes.com/ui/docs/charts/cartesian)

Bar, Line, and Area charts for visualizing categorical data series.

Charts live in a **separate entry point** (`@innostes/ui/charts`) to ensure that applications not utilizing charts do not incur the bundle size cost of Recharts.

## Installation

Charts are built on top of [Recharts](https://recharts.org/). You must install it as a peer dependency alongside `@innostes/ui`.

**Important Version Guidance:**
Due to a transitive peer dependency conflict, you must match the Recharts version to your React version:
- **React 17:** Use Recharts **2.15.x** (`pnpm add recharts@^2.15.0`)
- **React 18 / 19:** Use Recharts **3.x** (`pnpm add recharts@^3.0.0`)

```bash
# For React 18 / 19
pnpm add recharts@^3.0.0

# For React 17
pnpm add recharts@^2.15.0
```

## Import

Explicitly import chart components from `@innostes/ui/charts`, **not** from `@innostes/ui` directly.

```tsx
import { BarChart, LineChart, AreaChart } from '@innostes/ui/charts';
```

## Accessibility

A core differentiator of our chart components is their built-in accessibility. Every chart renders an accessible, visually-hidden `<table>` alongside the visual SVG representation (via the internal `ChartFrame` wrapper).

This means screen reader users are not presented with an opaque graphic. Instead, they can navigate the actual tabular data using standard table commands, providing a significantly superior, first-class experience for assistive technology. The `aria-label` prop you provide is used to name this hidden table.

## Props Overview

- **`data`**: An array of objects representing your dataset.
- **`categoryKey`**: The key in your data objects that represents the categories along the X-axis (e.g., `'month'`, `'quarter'`).
- **`series`**: An array of objects defining which keys from the data to plot, shaped as `{ key: string, label: string }`. The `label` is used in legends and tooltips.
- **`valueFormatter`**: An optional function to format the numeric values (e.g., adding currency symbols) for tooltips and axes.
- **`locale`**: Passed to handle localization formatting within the accessible table and tooltips.
- **`aria-label`**: Required string to name the underlying hidden data table for screen readers.

## Theming & Interactions

Colors are automatically assigned from the `chart-1` to `chart-8` categorical tokens defined in `theme.css` and `dark.css`. You can also override colors per series using these tokens or semantic tones (e.g., `success`, `destructive`).

Legends are fully interactive out-of-the-box. Clicking a legend entry toggles the visibility of that data series. If a chart contains only a single series, the legend is automatically hidden to save space and reduce clutter.

## Bar Chart

<ComponentPreview name="charts/cartesian/bar" />

## Line Chart

<ComponentPreview name="charts/cartesian/line" />

## Area Chart

<ComponentPreview name="charts/cartesian/area" />

## API

<ApiTable components={['BarChart', 'LineChart', 'AreaChart']} />

## Donut Chart (https://innostes.com/ui/docs/charts/donut)

A Donut chart for visualizing proportions with a prominent center metric.

Charts live in a **separate entry point** (`@innostes/ui/charts`) to ensure that applications not utilizing charts do not incur the bundle size cost of Recharts.

## Installation

As with all charts, `DonutChart` requires Recharts as a peer dependency.

**Important Version Guidance:**
- **React 17:** Use Recharts **2.15.x** (`pnpm add recharts@^2.15.0`)
- **React 18 / 19:** Use Recharts **3.x** (`pnpm add recharts@^3.0.0`)

## Import

Explicitly import chart components from `@innostes/ui/charts`, **not** from `@innostes/ui` directly.

```tsx
import { DonutChart } from '@innostes/ui/charts';
```

## Accessibility

Just like Cartesian charts, the `DonutChart` automatically renders an accessible, visually-hidden `<table>` containing the raw data and percentage shares. This allows screen readers to navigate the data easily. The `aria-label` prop is required and is used to name this hidden table.

## Center Metric

The `DonutChart` supports a distinct API for displaying a prominent metric in the center of the ring via the `centerValue` and `centerLabel` props. This is ideal for highlighting the primary takeaway of the chart (e.g., total volume, overall percentage).

## Props Overview

- **`data`**: An array of slices to render, each defined as `{ key: string, label: string, value: number, color?: ChartColor }`.
- **`valueFormatter`**: Optional function to format the values displayed in tooltips and the accessible table.
- **`locale`**: Optional locale string for number formatting in the accessible table.
- **`aria-label`**: Required string to name the underlying hidden data table.

## Theming

Slices can be colored automatically using the `chart-1` to `chart-8` categorical tokens, or you can assign specific semantic tones like `success`, `destructive`, or `warning` to individual slices via the `color` property in the data objects.

## Usage

<ComponentPreview name="charts/donut/basic" />

## API

<ApiTable components={['DonutChart']} />

## Charts (https://innostes.com/ui/docs/charts/index)

Accessible, theme-aware charting primitives for financial summaries and inventory analytics.

import { CategoryGrid } from '@/components/docs/category-grid';

# Charts

Chart components deliver accessible, responsive data visualisations across Northwind Traders Pvt Ltd's executive dashboards and operational reports. Built on Recharts with semantic design tokens, they adapt automatically to light and dark themes.

## Components

<CategoryGrid category="charts" />

## Usage guidelines

- **Semantic colour assignment**: Use token-based palette colours rather than hardcoded hex codes to guarantee contrast in both light and dark themes.
- **Data alternatives**: Always provide accessible data tables or summary text alongside charts to ensure full accessibility for screen reader operators.
- **Formatters**: Use localized number and currency formatters (`Intl.NumberFormat`) for tooltip and axis ticks.

## Button Group (https://innostes.com/ui/docs/components/actions/button-group)

Segmented container joining adjacent buttons horizontally or vertically for pagers and split actions.

ButtonGroup organizes a collection of related button triggers into a cohesive segmented bar, collapsing adjacent borders and rounding only the outer corners. It is commonly used for date pagination controls, multi-part save buttons, and table view switchers.

<ComponentPreview name="actions/button-group/basic" />

## Import

```tsx
import { Button, ButtonGroup } from '@innostes/ui';
```

## When to use

- **Use ButtonGroup** when grouping related triggers such as pagination controls (Previous / Today / Next) or split action menus (Save / More options).
- **Use ToggleGroup** when buttons toggle pressed states or select mutually exclusive options.
- **Use FormActions** when laying out separate form submission buttons (e.g. Save and Cancel) across a footer.

## Examples

### Basic usage

Wrap adjacent buttons with `ButtonGroup` and assign an accessible label:

```tsx
<ButtonGroup aria-label="Order pagination">
  <Button variant="outline" size="sm">Previous</Button>
  <Button variant="outline" size="sm">Next</Button>
</ButtonGroup>
```

### Split button

Combine a primary action trigger with a contextual dropdown menu button:

```tsx
<ButtonGroup aria-label="Invoice settlement actions">
  <Button variant="primary">Approve and remit</Button>
  <Button
    variant="primary"
    iconOnly
    aria-label="Additional remittance options"
    className="border-s border-s-primary-foreground/20"
  >
    <ChevronDown className="size-4" />
  </Button>
</ButtonGroup>
```

### Orientation

Arrange buttons vertically when building sidebar toolbars:

```tsx
<ButtonGroup orientation="vertical" aria-label="Document view tools">
  <Button variant="outline" size="sm">Zoom in</Button>
  <Button variant="outline" size="sm">Zoom out</Button>
  <Button variant="outline" size="sm">Reset</Button>
</ButtonGroup>
```

## Accessibility

### Keyboard navigation

<KeyboardTable
  rows={[
    { key: 'Tab', action: 'Moves focus sequentially between the individual buttons inside the group.' },
    { key: 'Enter / Space', action: 'Activates the currently focused button.' },
  ]}
/>

### Screen readers and ARIA

- **`role="group"`**: Automatically applied to the wrapper container.
- **`aria-label` requirement**: You **must** provide `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` describing the collection of buttons (e.g. `aria-label="Pagination controls"`).
- **Z-index focus stacking**: Focus rings are rendered with elevated z-index so the active button outline is never clipped by neighbouring buttons.

## Guidelines

<DoDont>
  <Do>
    Always provide an `aria-label` on `ButtonGroup` explaining the shared purpose of the grouped actions.
  </Do>
  <Dont>
    Never use `ButtonGroup` for mutually exclusive selection; use `ToggleGroup` or `RadioGroup` instead.
  </Dont>
</DoDont>

<DoDont>
  <Do>
    Maintain consistent button variants and sizes inside a single group container.
  </Do>
  <Dont>
    Never mix conflicting heights (`size="sm"` with `size="lg"`) within the same button group.
  </Dont>
</DoDont>

## API reference

<ApiTable components={['ButtonGroup']} />

## Related

- [Button](/ui/docs/components/actions/button) — Individual interactive action trigger.
- [ToggleGroup](/ui/docs/components/actions/toggle-group) — Connected group of toggle buttons for selection states.
- [Pagination](/ui/docs/components/navigation/pagination) — High-level navigation control for multi-page data sets.

## Button (https://innostes.com/ui/docs/components/actions/button)

Foundation action trigger supporting multiple semantic variants, sizes, loading spinners, and render polymorphism.

import { ButtonPlayground } from '@/components/docs/button-playground';
import { VariantCards, SizesDemo, IconsDemo, LoadingDemo, DisabledDemo, AsLinkDemo } from '@/components/docs/button-demos';

Buttons allow users to execute single-tap operations, submit forms, confirm transactions, and trigger dialogues. Built on Base UI's button primitive, `@innostes/ui` buttons guarantee visible keyboard focus rings, proper disabled state semantics, and render polymorphism without invalid DOM nesting.

<ComponentPreview name="actions/button/basic" />

## Import

```tsx
import { Button, buttonVariants } from '@innostes/ui';
```

## When to use

- **Use Button** for operational actions such as saving records, approving purchase orders, opening modals, or deleting items.
- **Use Link or Button with `render`** when navigating to a new URL or page route.
- **Use ButtonGroup** when grouping closely related actions into a single segmented bar (e.g. Save, Save and submit).
- **Use Toggle or ToggleGroup** when switching a two-state option on or off, or selecting from a mutual exclusion set.

## Anatomy

<Anatomy
  slots={[
    { name: 'root', description: 'The outer button element (native button or custom render element)', dataSlot: 'button' },
    { name: 'spinner', description: 'Animated loading indicator rendered during active state', dataSlot: 'button-spinner' },
    { name: 'start-icon', description: 'Leading icon slot aligned with typography', dataSlot: 'button-icon-start' },
    { name: 'end-icon', description: 'Trailing icon slot aligned with typography', dataSlot: 'button-icon-end' },
  ]}
/>

## Examples

### Interactive playground

Experiment with button props, variants, and interactive states:

<ButtonPlayground />

### Variants

Use `variant` to express visual hierarchy:

<VariantCards />

```tsx
<Button variant="primary">Approve PO</Button>
<Button variant="secondary">Filter view</Button>
<Button variant="outline">Export CSV</Button>
<Button variant="ghost">Cancel</Button>
<Button variant="destructive">Void invoice</Button>
<Button variant="link">Terms of supply</Button>
```

### Sizes

Choose from three standardized heights: `sm` (32px), `md` (40px, default), and `lg` (48px):

<SizesDemo />

```tsx
<Button size="sm">Compact (32px)</Button>
<Button size="md">Default (40px)</Button>
<Button size="lg">Large (48px)</Button>
```

### With icons

Add leading or trailing icons using `startIcon` and `endIcon`. For icon-only triggers, use `iconOnly` alongside an explicit `aria-label`:

<IconsDemo />

### Loading state

Display a spinning indicator and prevent accidental duplicate submissions:

<LoadingDemo />

### Disabled state

Deactivate interactions during invalid preconditions:

<DisabledDemo />

### As link

Render the button visually while rendering an underlying framework router link:

<AsLinkDemo />

## Accessibility

### Keyboard navigation

<KeyboardTable
  rows={[
    { key: 'Enter', action: 'Triggers the button click action or submits the enclosing form.' },
    { key: 'Space', action: 'Triggers the button click action and emits active button states.' },
    { key: 'Tab', action: 'Moves keyboard focus onto or away from the button in sequential reading order.' },
  ]}
/>

### Screen readers and ARIA

- **Native `<button>` element**: Guarantees standard button accessibility semantics in the accessibility tree.
- **Icon-only requirement**: When `iconOnly` is enabled, an accessible name **must** be provided via `aria-label`.
- **Loading state**: When `loading={true}` is set, the button receives `aria-busy="true"` and `disabled={true}`, preventing duplicate network invocations.

## Guidelines

<DoDont>
  <Do>
    Use descriptive, action-oriented verbs such as "Approve purchase order", "Save changes", or "Void invoice".
  </Do>
  <Dont>
    Never use vague labels such as "Click here", "Submit", or "OK" on enterprise action buttons.
  </Dont>
</DoDont>

<DoDont>
  <Do>
    Always supply an `aria-label` when using the `iconOnly` prop so screen readers describe the operation.
  </Do>
  <Dont>
    Never leave icon-only buttons unlabelled, or use decorative icons that duplicate neighbouring text labels.
  </Dont>
</DoDont>

## Actions (https://innostes.com/ui/docs/components/actions/index)

Core interactive controls for submitting forms, triggering commands, and toggling states.

import { CategoryGrid } from '@/components/docs/category-grid';

# Actions

Actions are the primary interactive building blocks across Northwind Traders Pvt Ltd's enterprise operations. They communicate intent, submit forms, open dialogs, and toggle feature states with clear visual feedback and full keyboard accessibility.

## Components

<CategoryGrid category="components/actions" />

## Usage guidelines

- **Hierarchy**: Use primary buttons for the main action on a screen (at most one primary action per view). Secondary and outline buttons accommodate alternative paths.
- **Icon placement**: Use start icons for directional or verb cues (e.g. "Export", "Add item"). Use end icons for continuation cues (e.g. "Next", "View details").
- **State indicators**: Always provide loading states for asynchronous API operations to prevent duplicate form submissions and maintain user certainty.

---

## Toggle Group (https://innostes.com/ui/docs/components/actions/toggle-group)

Segmented control managing single or multiple active states with roving tabindex and arrow-key navigation.

ToggleGroup coordinates a set of two-state toggle buttons. Built on Base UI's toggle group primitive, it supports both single-selection (e.g. text alignment, view modes) and multi-selection (e.g. text formatting options) with built-in roving focus management and keyboard arrow navigation.

<ComponentPreview name="actions/toggle-group/basic" />

## Import

```tsx
import { ToggleGroup, ToggleGroupItem } from '@innostes/ui';
```

## When to use

- **Use ToggleGroup** when users need to switch between related view layouts (e.g. List vs Grid) or apply multiple independent formatting options (e.g. Bold, Italic, Underline).
- **Use RadioGroup** when selecting one option from a list within a standard form where standard radio button styling is required.
- **Use Tabs** when selecting an option switches an entire underlying panel or page view.
- **Use ButtonGroup** when grouping operational action buttons that trigger commands rather than maintaining state.

## Examples

### Single selection

In default mode, ToggleGroup operates with single selection:

```tsx
const [view, setView] = useState(['table']);

<ToggleGroup value={view} onValueChange={setView} aria-label="Inventory layout">
  <ToggleGroupItem value="table">Table view</ToggleGroupItem>
  <ToggleGroupItem value="kanban">Kanban board</ToggleGroupItem>
</ToggleGroup>
```

### Multiple selection

Enable the `multiple` prop to permit selecting more than one option concurrently:

```tsx
const [formatting, setFormatting] = useState(['bold', 'italic']);

<ToggleGroup
  multiple
  value={formatting}
  onValueChange={setFormatting}
  aria-label="Rich text formatting"
>
  <ToggleGroupItem value="bold" aria-label="Bold"><Bold className="size-4" /></ToggleGroupItem>
  <ToggleGroupItem value="italic" aria-label="Italic"><Italic className="size-4" /></ToggleGroupItem>
  <ToggleGroupItem value="underline" aria-label="Underline"><Underline className="size-4" /></ToggleGroupItem>
</ToggleGroup>
```

### Attached outline styling

Use `variant="outline"` to merge borders and join the items into a solid segmented control:

```tsx
<ToggleGroup variant="outline" defaultValue={['all']} aria-label="Status filter">
  <ToggleGroupItem value="all">All orders</ToggleGroupItem>
  <ToggleGroupItem value="pending">Pending</ToggleGroupItem>
  <ToggleGroupItem value="dispatched">Dispatched</ToggleGroupItem>
</ToggleGroup>
```

## Accessibility

### Keyboard navigation

<KeyboardTable
  rows={[
    { key: 'ArrowRight / ArrowDown', action: 'Moves focus to the next item in the group, wrapping to the start.' },
    { key: 'ArrowLeft / ArrowUp', action: 'Moves focus to the previous item in the group, wrapping to the end.' },
    { key: 'Space / Enter', action: 'Toggles the pressed state of the currently focused item.' },
    { key: 'Home / End', action: 'Jumps focus directly to the first or last item in the group.' },
    { key: 'Tab', action: 'Leaves the toggle group and moves focus to the next control outside the group.' },
  ]}
/>

### Screen readers and ARIA

- **Roving tabindex**: Only the active or focused item has `tabIndex={0}`; remaining items receive `tabIndex={-1}`, ensuring the entire group acts as a single tab stop in the DOM.
- **`role="group"`**: Automatically applied to the container alongside the provided `aria-label`.
- **`aria-pressed`**: Emitted on each item to announce active state changes to screen readers.

## Guidelines

<DoDont>
  <Do>
    Always provide an `aria-label` on `ToggleGroup` describing the group purpose (e.g. `aria-label="View mode"`).
  </Do>
  <Dont>
    Never use `ToggleGroup` for navigating between separate URLs; use `Tabs` or standard navigation links instead.
  </Dont>
</DoDont>

<DoDont>
  <Do>
    Provide an `aria-label` on each `ToggleGroupItem` when items contain only icons without text labels.
  </Do>
  <Dont>
    Never mix mutually exclusive options with multi-select toggles inside the same group container.
  </Dont>
</DoDont>

## API reference

<ApiTable components={['ToggleGroup', 'ToggleGroupItem']} baseUi="toggle-group" />

- [Tabs](/ui/docs/components/navigation/tabs) — Tabbed interface for swapping content panels.

## Toggle (https://innostes.com/ui/docs/components/actions/toggle)

Accessible two-state pressed button primitive for formatting toolbars, favorites, and view modes.

Toggle is a two-state interactive control built on Base UI's toggle primitive. Unlike a standard button that triggers an action and immediately resets, Toggle maintains a pressed or unpressed state reflected via `aria-pressed`. It is ideal for rich text editor toolbars, bookmarking records, and filtering table views.

<ComponentPreview name="actions/toggle/basic" />

## Import

```tsx
import { Toggle, toggleVariants } from '@innostes/ui';
```

## When to use

- **Use Toggle** for binary options where the button itself displays its active state (e.g. bold formatting, bookmarking an invoice).
- **Use Switch** for binary preferences inside configuration forms where a toggle switch with a distinct track and thumb is expected.
- **Use Checkbox** for multi-item selection in data tables or form agreements.
- **Use ToggleGroup** when grouping multiple toggle buttons into a toolbar or single-choice segmented control.

## Examples

### Basic usage

Toggle supports both uncontrolled (`defaultPressed`) and controlled (`pressed`, `onPressedChange`) modes:

```tsx
// Uncontrolled
<Toggle defaultPressed aria-label="Toggle bold text">
  <Bold className="size-4" />
</Toggle>

// Controlled
<Toggle
  pressed={isBookmarked}
  onPressedChange={setIsBookmarked}
  aria-label="Bookmark purchase order"
>
  <Bookmark className="size-4" />
</Toggle>
```

### With text label

Toggles can pair icons with visible textual descriptions:

```tsx
<Toggle variant="outline" aria-label="Mark invoice as urgent">
  <AlertCircle className="size-4 me-1.5 text-amber-500" />
  <span>Mark urgent</span>
</Toggle>
```

### Sizes

Toggles support the standard `sm` (32px), `md` (40px, default), and `lg` (48px) size scale:

```tsx
<Toggle size="sm" aria-label="Compact toggle"><Pin className="size-3.5" /></Toggle>
<Toggle size="md" aria-label="Default toggle"><Pin className="size-4" /></Toggle>
<Toggle size="lg" aria-label="Large toggle"><Pin className="size-5" /></Toggle>
```

## Accessibility

### Keyboard navigation

<KeyboardTable
  rows={[
    { key: 'Space', action: 'Toggles the pressed state between on and off.' },
    { key: 'Enter', action: 'Toggles the pressed state between on and off.' },
    { key: 'Tab', action: 'Moves focus to the toggle or away to the next interactive control.' },
  ]}
/>

### Screen readers and ARIA

- **`aria-pressed`**: Emits `aria-pressed="true"` when active and `aria-pressed="false"` when inactive. Screen readers announce "pressed" or "not pressed" immediately.
- **Icon-only requirement**: When a toggle contains only an icon glyph, an accessible name **must** be provided via `aria-label`.
- **Disabled state**: Applies `disabled` and `aria-disabled="true"` to prevent state changes.

## Guidelines

<DoDont>
  <Do>
    Provide an `aria-label` describing the state being toggled when no visible text is present (e.g. `aria-label="Toggle italic text"`).
  </Do>
  <Dont>
    Never use `Toggle` for irreversible operational actions such as deleting records or submitting forms; use `Button` instead.
  </Dont>
</DoDont>

<DoDont>
  <Do>
    Use `Toggle` when changes take effect immediately without requiring a separate "Save" form submission.
  </Do>
  <Dont>
    Never nest a `Toggle` inside a standard form where users expect explicit submit button confirmation.
  </Dont>
</DoDont>

## API reference

<ApiTable components={['Toggle']} baseUi="toggle" />

- [ToggleGroup](/ui/docs/components/actions/toggle-group) — Grouped collection of toggle buttons for toolbar selection.
- [Switch](/ui/docs/components/forms/switch) — Binary on/off control with physical switch semantics.
- [Button](/ui/docs/components/actions/button) — Foundation action trigger.

---

## Avatar (https://innostes.com/ui/docs/components/data-display/avatar)

Image with initials fallback, four sizes, round or square, and stacked groups.

<ComponentPreview name="data-display/avatar/basic" />

## Import

```tsx
import { Avatar, AvatarImage, AvatarFallback, AvatarGroup } from '@innostes/ui';
```

## Usage

```tsx
<Avatar>
  <AvatarImage src={user.photoUrl} alt="" />
  <AvatarFallback>{initials(user.name)}</AvatarFallback>
</Avatar>
```

The fallback shows while the image loads and if it fails. Use `delay` on `AvatarFallback` (ms) to
avoid a flash of initials on fast connections.

## Accessibility

- When the person's name is shown next to the avatar, use `alt=""` so it isn't read twice.
- `AvatarGroup` labels its "+N" counter (e.g. "2 more").

## API Reference

<ApiTable components={['Avatar', 'AvatarImage', 'AvatarFallback', 'AvatarGroup']} baseUi="avatar" />

## Badge (https://innostes.com/ui/docs/components/data-display/badge)

Semantic colours for statuses, with an optional dot.

<ComponentPreview name="data-display/badge/basic" />

## Import

```tsx
import { Badge, badgeVariants } from '@innostes/ui';
```

## Usage

Map your domain statuses to a variant once, and reuse it:

```tsx
const statusVariant = {
  paid: 'success',
  pending: 'warning',
  overdue: 'destructive',
  draft: 'info',
} as const satisfies Record<InvoiceStatus, BadgeVariant>;

<Badge variant={statusVariant[invoice.status]} dot>{invoice.status}</Badge>
```

Don't rely on colour alone: the text says what the status is.

## API Reference

<ApiTable components={['Badge']} />

## Data Table (https://innostes.com/ui/docs/components/data-display/data-table)

Sorting, row selection, pagination, loading and empty states. Client-side or server-side.

<ComponentPreview name="data-display/data-table/basic" align="start" />

## Import

```tsx
import { DataTable, type DataTableColumn, type SortState } from '@innostes/ui';
```

## Columns

Columns are typed against your row type. `accessor` returns the raw value (used for sorting and
as the default cell text); `cell` renders anything.

```tsx
const columns: DataTableColumn<Invoice>[] = [
  { id: 'number', header: 'Invoice', accessor: (r) => r.number, sortable: true },
  { id: 'status', header: 'Status', cell: (r) => <Badge variant={tone[r.status]}>{r.status}</Badge> },
  {
    id: 'amount',
    header: 'Amount',
    accessor: (r) => r.amount,
    sortable: true,
    align: 'end',
    cell: (r) => money.format(r.amount),
  },
];

<DataTable aria-label="Invoices" data={invoices} columns={columns} getRowId={(r) => r.id} />
```

Sorting is natural and locale-aware ("Item 2" before "Item 10"); dates and numbers sort by value;
empty values always go last.

## Selection, sorting and pagination

Each piece of state can be uncontrolled (`defaultSort`, `defaultSelectedIds`, `defaultPage`) or
controlled (`sort` + `onSortChange`, `selectedIds` + `onSelectedIdsChange`, `page` + `onPageChange`),
so you can keep it in the URL or a store.

```tsx
<DataTable
  aria-label="Orders"
  data={orders}
  columns={columns}
  getRowId={(o) => o.id}
  selectable
  selectedIds={selected}
  onSelectedIdsChange={setSelected}
  defaultSort={{ columnId: 'date', direction: 'desc' }}
  pageSize={20}
/>
```

## Server-side data

Turn on `manualSorting` and `manualPagination`, pass the current page of rows as `data`, and fetch
in the change handlers. `totalCount` tells the table how many pages exist.

```tsx
const [sort, setSort] = useState<SortState | null>({ columnId: 'date', direction: 'desc' });
const [page, setPage] = useState(1);
const { data, isLoading } = useOrders({ sort, page, pageSize: 20 }); // your data hook

<DataTable
  aria-label="Orders"
  data={data?.rows ?? []}
  totalCount={data?.total}
  columns={columns}
  getRowId={(o) => o.id}
  manualSorting
  sort={sort}
  onSortChange={setSort}
  manualPagination
  page={page}
  onPageChange={setPage}
  pageSize={20}
  loading={isLoading}
/>
```

## Loading and empty states

<ComponentPreview name="data-display/data-table/loading" align="start" />

## Accessibility

- Real `<table>` markup with `aria-sort` on sortable headers and sort buttons inside them.
- The table needs a name: pass `aria-label`.
- Selection checkboxes are labelled; the selected count is announced politely.
- `onRowClick` is for convenience only. Keep the same action reachable by keyboard (e.g. a link in
  the first cell, or the row actions menu).

## API Reference

<ApiTable components={['DataTable']} />

`DataTableColumn<TRow>` fields: `id`, `header`, `accessor`, `cell`, `sortable`, `align`, `width`,
`className`, `headerClassName`. They're documented with TSDoc, so your editor shows them on hover.

---

## Empty State (https://innostes.com/ui/docs/components/data-display/empty-state)

<ComponentPreview name="data-display/empty-state/basic" />

```tsx
import { EmptyState } from '@innostes/ui';
```

Say what's empty, why, and what to do next:

- **First use**: "No invoices yet" + "Create invoice".

## Icon Tile (https://innostes.com/ui/docs/components/data-display/icon-tile)

14 colours, soft or solid, four sizes. Used by metric cards, lists and feature grids.

<ComponentPreview name="data-display/icon-tile/basic" />

## Import

```tsx
import { IconTile, type IconTileTone } from '@innostes/ui';
```

## Usage

```tsx
<IconTile tone="chart-2"><UsersIcon /></IconTile>
<IconTile tone="success" variant="solid" shape="circle" size="sm"><CheckIcon /></IconTile>
```

- **Semantic tones** (`primary`, `success`, `warning`, `destructive`, `info`, `neutral`) carry meaning.
- **Categorical tones** (`chart-1` … `chart-8`) tell items apart, e.g. one colour per module.
  They're the same colours the charts use, so a module looks the same everywhere.
- The tile is decorative (`aria-hidden`); put the meaning in the text next to it.

## API Reference

## Data display (https://innostes.com/ui/docs/components/data-display/index)

Components for structured record presentation, hierarchies, and metric highlights.

import { CategoryGrid } from '@/components/docs/category-grid';

# Data display

Data display components structure and present information with high information density, clear typographic hierarchy, and accessible markup. From high-throughput financial tables to hierarchical organizational trees, these components present Northwind Traders Pvt Ltd's operational data with clarity.

## Components

<CategoryGrid category="components/data-display" />

## Best practices

- **Data tables**: Prefer `DataTable` for complex administrative tables requiring client-side pagination, sorting, row selection, and column toggling.
- **Empty states**: Always render an explicit `EmptyState` when collections, search queries, or filter combinations produce zero results.
- **Status indicators**: Use semantic badges (`success`, `warning`, `destructive`) consistently across data rows to reflect item lifecycles.

## Stat (https://innostes.com/ui/docs/components/data-display/stat)

Label, value and trend, with colours that know whether "up" is good.

<ComponentPreview name="data-display/stat/basic" />

## Import

```tsx
import { Stat } from '@innostes/ui';
```

## Usage

```tsx
<Stat label="Revenue" value="€48,250" delta="+12.5%" helper="vs last month" />
<Stat label="Churn" value="2.1%" delta="+0.4%" upIsGood={false} />
```

- `trend` is inferred from a leading `+` or `-` in `delta`; pass it explicitly when `delta` isn't a string.

## Tree View (https://innostes.com/ui/docs/components/data-display/tree-view)

Departments, chart of accounts, categories and folders, with full WAI-ARIA tree keyboard support.

<ComponentPreview name="data-display/tree-view/basic" />

## Import

```tsx
import { TreeView, type TreeNode } from '@innostes/ui';
```

## Usage

Pass nested `TreeNode`s. A node with `children` (even an empty array) can be expanded.

```tsx
const accounts: TreeNode[] = [
  {
    id: 'assets',
    label: 'Assets',
    children: [
      { id: 'cash', label: 'Cash', meta: '₹4.2L' },
      { id: 'ar', label: 'Accounts receivable', meta: '₹12.8L' },
    ],
  },
];

<TreeView
  aria-label="Chart of accounts"
  items={accounts}
  expanded={expanded}
  onExpandedChange={setExpanded}
  selected={account}
  onSelectedChange={setAccount}
/>
```

- `icon` goes before the label, `meta` (a count, an amount) at the end.
- `disabled` nodes can be focused but not selected.
- For lazy loading, give a node `children: []`, load its children in `onExpandedChange`, then update `items`.

## Keyboard

| Key | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Up / Down | Previous / next visible node |
| Right | Expand; if expanded, go to the first child |
| Left | Collapse; if collapsed, go to the parent |
| Home / End | First / last visible node |
| Enter / Space | Select |
| Letters | Jump to the next node starting with them |

## API Reference

<ApiTable components={['TreeView']} />

Info, success, warning and error messages with matching icons and live-region roles.

  Override with `role` if needed.

## Gauge (https://innostes.com/ui/docs/components/feedback/gauge)

KPI dials for budget use, capacity, SLA and quota, with value-based colours.

<ComponentPreview name="feedback/gauge/basic" />

## Import

```tsx
import { Gauge } from '@innostes/ui';
```

## Usage

```tsx
<Gauge
  value={82}
  label="Budget used"
  description="₹49L of ₹60L"
  format={{ style: 'percent' }}
  tone={(v) => (v > 90 ? 'destructive' : v > 75 ? 'warning' : 'success')}
/>
```

- `min` and `max` set the range (default 0–100). `format` takes `Intl.NumberFormat` options.
- Without `format`, or with `style: 'percent'`, the number shown is the share of the range (312 of 400 shows "78%"). Other formats, e.g. `{ style: 'currency', currency: 'INR' }`, apply to the value itself.
- `tone` is a colour, or a function of the value for thresholds.
- `size` sets the width (default `10rem`).
- For a compact bar, use [Meter](/ui/docs/components/feedback/meter). For task progress, use [Progress](/ui/docs/components/feedback/progress).

## Accessibility

Built on Base UI's Meter: it has `role="meter"`, is named by `label` (or `aria-label`), and exposes the value and range. The arc is decorative.

## API Reference

<ApiTable components={['Gauge']} />

---

## Feedback (https://innostes.com/ui/docs/components/feedback/index)

Components for communicating system status, background task progress, and operation outcomes.

import { CategoryGrid } from '@/components/docs/category-grid';

# Feedback

Feedback components keep operators at Northwind Traders Pvt Ltd informed about task status, background processes, system health, and operational outcomes. They provide immediate, accessible status communication across the platform.

## Components

<CategoryGrid category="components/feedback" />

## Usage guidelines

- **Tone matching**: Use info for contextual guidance, success for completed operations, warning for non-blocking concerns, and destructive/error for failed tasks or critical disruptions.
- **Duration**: Reserve persistent banners (`Alert`) for system-wide notices or section errors that require resolution. Use transient toasts (`Toast`) for operation confirmations.
- **Accessibility**: All feedback components emit appropriate ARIA live regions (`polite` for progress/alerts, `assertive` for urgent errors) and support high-contrast mode tokens.

## Toast (https://innostes.com/ui/docs/components/feedback/toast)

Success, error, warning, loading and promise toasts with actions, swipe to dismiss and a queue limit.

<ComponentPreview name="feedback/toast/basic" />

## Setup

Mount `Toaster` once, near the root of your app:

```tsx title="app/layout.tsx"
import { Toaster } from '@innostes/ui';

export default function RootLayout({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) {
  return (
    <html lang="en">
      <body>
        {children}
        <Toaster position="bottom-right" />
      </body>
    </html>
  );
}
```

## Usage

`toast` works anywhere, including outside React (API clients, stores, event handlers):

```tsx
import { toast } from '@innostes/ui';

toast('Order archived', { action: { label: 'Undo', onClick: restore } });
toast.success('Invoice sent');
toast.error('Could not save', { description: error.message });

// Loading → success / error
await toast.promise(saveOrder(), {
  loading: 'Saving order…',
  success: (order) => `${order.id} saved`,
  error: (err) => `Failed: ${err.message}`,
});

// Manual control
const id = toast.loading('Uploading…');
toast.update(id, { title: 'Uploaded', type: 'success', timeout: 4000 });
toast.dismiss(id);
```

## Accessibility

- Toasts are announced politely; `error` toasts use high priority and are announced immediately.
- Keyboard users can jump to the toasts with <kbd>F6</kbd>. Toasts pause while hovered or focused.
- Toasts disappear, so don't put anything the user must act on only in a toast. Use an
  [Alert](/ui/docs/components/feedback/alert) for that.

## API Reference

<ApiTable components={['Toaster']} baseUi="toast" />

`toast(title, options)` options: `description`, `type`, `timeout` (ms, `0` = until dismissed),
`priority`, `action` (`{ label, onClick }`) and `onClose`.

---

## Calendar (https://innostes.com/ui/docs/components/forms/calendar)

Single and range modes, min/max bounds, disabled dates, one or two month views, and Intl-based locale formatting.

<ComponentPreview name="forms/calendar/basic" />

## Import

```tsx
import { Calendar, type DateRange, type Weekday } from '@innostes/ui';
```

## When to use

Use `Calendar` when users need to see an inline month view to choose a single calendar day or an inclusive date range:

- Displaying booking schedules, dispatch timetables, or delivery cutoffs directly on an ERP dashboard.
- Selecting ranges across one or two months when visualising calendar context is essential.
- Building custom date filter panels.

When choosing between date selection patterns:
- Use [Date Picker](/ui/docs/components/forms/date-picker) if the calendar should appear within a compact popover triggered from a form field or table toolbar.
- Use [Date Range Picker](/ui/docs/components/forms/date-picker#date-range-picker-with-presets) if you need preset ranges (such as "Last 30 days" or "This quarter") attached to a popover trigger.
- Use [Input](/ui/docs/components/forms/input) with `type="date"` only when native mobile OS date pickers are explicitly preferred over consistent cross-browser styling.

## Examples

### Single date

By default, `Calendar` runs in single-date mode (`mode="single"`). Provide `value` and `onValueChange` for controlled operation.

```tsx
'use client';

import { useState } from 'react';
import { Calendar } from '@innostes/ui';

export function DispatchDateSelector() {
  const [dispatchDate, setDispatchDate] = useState<Date | null>(new Date());

  return (
    <Calendar
      value={dispatchDate}
      onValueChange={setDispatchDate}
      aria-label="Dispatch schedule"
    />
  );
}
```

### Date range

Set `mode="range"` to allow selecting a start date and an end date. Setting `numberOfMonths={2}` renders two consecutive months side-by-side, which simplifies picking cross-month accounting or reporting cycles.

```tsx
'use client';

import { useState } from 'react';
import { Calendar, type DateRange } from '@innostes/ui';

export function AuditRangeCalendar() {
  const [range, setRange] = useState<DateRange>({
    from: new Date(2026, 3, 1),
    to: new Date(2026, 3, 15),
  });

  return (
    <Calendar
      mode="range"
      numberOfMonths={2}
      value={range}
      onValueChange={setRange}
      aria-label="Audit observation period"
    />
  );
}
```

### Date constraints and disabled dates

Pass `min` and `max` bounds to prevent selecting dates outside allowable fiscal limits. Use `isDateDisabled` to disable specific calendar dates, such as gazetted public holidays or weekend warehouse closures.

```tsx
import { Calendar } from '@innostes/ui';

const isWeekend = (date: Date) => date.getDay() === 0 || date.getDay() === 6;

export function WarehouseCutoffCalendar() {
  return (
    <Calendar
      min={new Date(2026, 0, 1)}
      max={new Date(2026, 11, 31)}
      isDateDisabled={isWeekend}
      aria-label="Warehouse loading date"
    />
  );
}
```

### Dropdown year and month navigation

For dates far in the past or future (such as incorporation dates or employee date of birth), set `captionLayout="dropdown"`. This substitutes plain month header text with accessible select dropdowns for rapid jumping.

```tsx
import { Calendar } from '@innostes/ui';

export function IncorporationCalendar() {
  return (
    <Calendar
      captionLayout="dropdown"
      fromYear={1990}
      toYear={2030}
      aria-label="Entity incorporation date"
    />
  );
}
```

### Locale and week start

Month and weekday labels automatically derive from the user's browser runtime through `Intl.DateTimeFormat`. You can pass an explicit BCP 47 locale tag (`locale="en-IN"`) or override the first day of the week with `weekStartsOn` (where `0` is Sunday and `1` is Monday).

```tsx
import { Calendar } from '@innostes/ui';

export function IndianFiscalCalendar() {
  return (
    <Calendar
      locale="en-IN"
      weekStartsOn={1}
      aria-label="GST filing schedule"
    />
  );
}
```

### Time zones

`Calendar` operates strictly on **local calendar days**:
- Values are native JavaScript `Date` instances clamped to midnight in the local browser runtime.
- The component does not apply UTC hour offsets or time zone translations.
- When sending values to an ERP API, serialise the calendar day to an ISO date string format (`YYYY-MM-DD`) at the application boundary, rather than sending a raw UTC timestamp that could shift the calendar day across midnight in eastern or western longitudes.

## Accessibility

`Calendar` implements the W3C WAI-ARIA Date Picker Grid design pattern.

### Keyboard navigation

The calendar grid is a single tab stop with roving tabindex across days.

<KeyboardTable
  entries={[
    { key: 'Left Arrow', action: 'Moves focus to the previous day.' },
    { key: 'Right Arrow', action: 'Moves focus to the next day.' },
    { key: 'Up Arrow', action: 'Moves focus to the same weekday in the previous week.' },
    { key: 'Down Arrow', action: 'Moves focus to the same weekday in the next week.' },
    { key: 'Home', action: 'Moves focus to the first day of the current week.' },
    { key: 'End', action: 'Moves focus to the last day of the current week.' },
    { key: 'Page Up', action: 'Navigates to the previous month.' },
    { key: 'Page Down', action: 'Navigates to the next month.' },
    { key: 'Shift + Page Up', action: 'Navigates to the previous calendar year.' },
    { key: 'Shift + Page Down', action: 'Navigates to the next calendar year.' },
    { key: 'Enter / Space', action: 'Selects the currently focused day.' },
  ]}
/>

### Screen readers

- The month table uses `role="grid"` with column headers denoting abbreviated and full weekday names (`abbr` attribute).
- Each cell has a full textual accessible label (e.g., "Thursday, 15 October 2026").
- The current calendar date is marked with `aria-current="date"`.
- Selected dates communicate their status through `aria-selected="true"`.
- Disabled days maintain keyboard focusability to allow navigating across weeks without breaking roving focus, marked with `aria-disabled="true"`.

## Guidelines

<DoDont
  do={{
    description: 'Clamp dates to midnight (00:00:00) in local time when computing boundaries to avoid subtle 1-hour daylight saving or offset mismatches.',
    code: `const start = new Date(2026, 3, 1, 0, 0, 0, 0);`,
  }}
  dont={{
    description: 'Do not pass raw UTC timestamps from an API directly into min or max props without converting to local calendar days.',
    code: `// Can cause boundary skew across timezones\n<Calendar min={new Date('2026-04-01T00:00:00.000Z')} />`,
  }}
/>

<DoDont
  do={{
    description: 'Use `numberOfMonths={2}` when rendering range mode on desktop screens so users can inspect start and end dates spanning consecutive months.',
    code: `<Calendar mode="range" numberOfMonths={2} value={range} onValueChange={setRange} />`,
  }}
  dont={{
    description: 'Do not use multi-month layouts inside narrow mobile dialogs or sidebars where horizontal scrolling would be required.',
    code: `<div className="w-64">\n  <Calendar numberOfMonths={2} />\n</div>`,
  }}
/>

## API reference

<ApiTable components={['Calendar']} />

## Related

- [Date Picker](/ui/docs/components/forms/date-picker) — Popover-wrapped calendar for form inputs.
- [Field](/ui/docs/components/forms/field) — Accessible container with labels, descriptions, and error messages.
- [Locale Selects](/ui/docs/components/forms/locale-select) — Regional preference dropdowns for timezones, countries, and date formats.

## Checkbox (https://innostes.com/ui/docs/components/forms/checkbox)

Accessible checkbox primitive supporting single agreement boxes, multi-select tables, and indeterminate "select all" parent groups.

import { CheckboxPlayground } from '@/components/docs/checkbox-playground';

`Checkbox` allows users to select one or multiple items from a list, toggle optional settings, or confirm legal agreements. Built on Base UI's checkbox primitive, it supports three visual and semantic states: checked, unchecked, and indeterminate (mixed).

<ComponentPreview name="forms/checkbox/basic" />

## Import

```tsx
import { Checkbox, CheckboxGroup } from '@innostes/ui';
```

## When to use

- **Use Checkbox** when users can select multiple options independently from a list, or toggle an isolated agreement (e.g. "I accept the delivery terms").
- **Use Switch** for binary options that take effect immediately without requiring form submission.
- **Use RadioGroup** when users must choose exactly one option from a mutually exclusive set.

## Examples

### Interactive playground

Experiment with checked, indeterminate, and disabled states:

<CheckboxPlayground />

### Single checkbox in a field

Wrap a checkbox inside `<Field>` with an accessible label:

```tsx
<Field>
  <label className="flex items-center gap-2.5 text-sm cursor-pointer">
    <Checkbox name="expressDelivery" />
    <span>Enable express carrier dispatch (Karnataka Hub)</span>
  </label>
  <FieldDescription>Guarantees delivery within 24 hours.</FieldDescription>
</Field>
```

### Indeterminate select all group

`CheckboxGroup` coordinates multiple child checkboxes and exposes a parent "select all" trigger that enters an indeterminate state when a partial subset of rows is selected:

<ComponentPreview name="forms/checkbox/group" />

```tsx
<CheckboxGroup
  value={selectedOrders}
  onValueChange={setSelectedOrders}
  allValues={['PO-101', 'PO-102', 'PO-103']}
>
  {({ isAllSelected, isSomeSelected, selectAll, unselectAll }) => (
    <div className="space-y-3">
      <label className="flex items-center gap-2 font-medium">
        <Checkbox
          checked={isAllSelected}
          indeterminate={isSomeSelected && !isAllSelected}
          onCheckedChange={(checked) => (checked ? selectAll() : unselectAll())}
        />
        <span>Select all purchase orders</span>
      </label>
      <div className="ms-6 space-y-2">
        <label className="flex items-center gap-2 text-sm">
          <Checkbox value="PO-101" /> PO-101 (₹45,000)
        </label>
        <label className="flex items-center gap-2 text-sm">
          <Checkbox value="PO-102" /> PO-102 (₹82,400)
        </label>
      </div>
    </div>
  )}
</CheckboxGroup>
```

## Accessibility

### Keyboard navigation

<KeyboardTable
  rows={[
    { key: 'Space', action: 'Toggles the checkbox between checked and unchecked.' },
    { key: 'Tab', action: 'Moves focus to the checkbox or moves to the next focusable element.' },
  ]}
/>

### Screen readers and ARIA

- **`role="checkbox"`**: Emits standard checkbox semantics.
- **`aria-checked`**: Sets `aria-checked="true"`, `false`, or `"mixed"` when in the indeterminate state.
- **Label coupling**: Wrapping the checkbox inside `<label>` or associating via `aria-label` ensures screen readers announce the label clearly upon focus.

## Guidelines

<DoDont>
  <Do>
    Use positive phrasing for checkbox labels (e.g. "Send shipment status notifications via SMS").
  </Do>
  <Dont>
    Never use negative phrasing such as "Do not notify me via SMS" which creates double-negative confusion.
  </Dont>
</DoDont>

<DoDont>
  <Do>
    Use the indeterminate state exclusively on parent checkboxes to indicate partial selection of a child set.
  </Do>
  <Dont>
    Never use indeterminate as an independent "maybe" or "unknown" choice for standalone user input.
  </Dont>
</DoDont>

## API reference

<ApiTable components={['Checkbox', 'CheckboxGroup']} baseUi="checkbox" />

## Related

- [Switch](/ui/docs/components/forms/switch) — Instant-acting binary switch toggle.
- [RadioGroup](/ui/docs/components/forms/radio-group) — Mutually exclusive option selection.
- [DataTable](/ui/docs/components/data-display/data-table) — High-density data grid with built-in checkbox row selection.

## Combobox (https://innostes.com/ui/docs/components/forms/combobox)

Accessible combobox input for filtering and selecting values from extensive or remote dataset collections.

`Combobox` combines a text input with a floating listbox popup. Built on Base UI's combobox primitive, it allows operators to type to filter large datasets, traverse options using arrow keys, and select records with keyboard or pointer input. It is designed for searching customer records, product SKUs, and general ledgers across Northwind Traders systems.

<ComponentPreview name="forms/combobox/basic" />

## Import

```tsx
import {
  Combobox,
  ComboboxInput,
  ComboboxContent,
  ComboboxList,
  ComboboxItem,
  ComboboxEmpty,
  ComboboxGroup,
  ComboboxGroupLabel,
  ComboboxSeparator,
} from '@innostes/ui';
```

## When to use

- **Use Combobox** when users need to filter through extensive datasets (50 to 10,000+ items) or query remote server endpoints asynchronously.
- **Use SearchableSelect** for moderate client-side lists (15 to 100 items) where a standard select trigger is preferred.
- **Use Select** when the list of options is short (under 15 items) and typing to filter is unnecessary.
- **Use TagInput** when users select and manage multiple tags or keywords concurrently.

### Selection control comparison

| Control | Selection count | Number of options | Search filter | Best suited for |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Combobox** | Single or Multi | 50 to 10,000+ | Yes | Large async remote datasets or autocomplete with custom item creation |
| **[SearchableSelect](/ui/docs/components/forms/searchable-select)** | Single | 15 to 100+ | Yes | Moderate lists requiring fast dropdown filter search |
| **[Select](/ui/docs/components/forms/select)** | Single or Multi | 5 to 15 | No (type-ahead) | Compact predefined lists (e.g. status, payment terms) |
| **[RadioGroup](/ui/docs/components/forms/radio-group)** | Single | 2 to 5 | No | Visible choices where side-by-side comparison is essential |
| **[TagInput](/ui/docs/components/forms/tag-input)** | Multi | Variable | Yes | Categorical metadata, SKU keywords, and multi-tag filtering |

## Examples

### Object collections with custom labels

When working with complex domain objects, supply `itemToStringLabel` to tell the combobox which property represents the human-readable string:

```tsx
interface Vendor {
  id: string;
  name: string;
  gstin: string;
}

const vendors: Vendor[] = [
  { id: 'v1', name: 'Hindustan Industrial Spares', gstin: '29AAAAA0000A1Z5' },
  { id: 'v2', name: 'Bharat Electricals Ltd', gstin: '29BBBBB1111B2Z6' },
];

<Combobox items={vendors} itemToStringLabel={(v) => v.name}>
  <ComboboxInput placeholder="Search supplier organisation..." />
  <ComboboxContent>
    <ComboboxEmpty>No vendor found.</ComboboxEmpty>
    <ComboboxList>
      {(vendor: Vendor) => (
        <ComboboxItem key={vendor.id} value={vendor}>
          <div>
            <div className="font-medium">{vendor.name}</div>
            <div className="text-xs text-muted-foreground font-mono">{vendor.gstin}</div>
          </div>
        </ComboboxItem>
      )}
    </ComboboxList>
  </ComboboxContent>
</Combobox>
```

### Server-side search filtering

Control input queries using `onInputValueChange` to query remote backend endpoints with debounced network calls:

```tsx
const [query, setQuery] = useState('');
const [items, setItems] = useState<Customer[]>([]);

<Combobox
  items={items}
  onInputValueChange={(val) => {
    setQuery(val);
    fetchCustomersDebounced(val).then(setItems);
  }}
>
  <ComboboxInput placeholder="Type customer name or GSTIN..." />
  <ComboboxContent>
    <ComboboxEmpty>No records matching search query.</ComboboxEmpty>
    <ComboboxList>
      {(item) => <ComboboxItem key={item.id} value={item}>{item.name}</ComboboxItem>}
    </ComboboxList>
  </ComboboxContent>
</Combobox>
```

## Accessibility

### Keyboard navigation

<KeyboardTable
  rows={[
    { key: 'ArrowDown', action: 'Opens the listbox if closed, or highlights the subsequent option.' },
    { key: 'ArrowUp', action: 'Highlights the preceding option, or closes the popup when at the top.' },
    { key: 'Enter', action: 'Selects the currently highlighted option and closes the listbox.' },
    { key: 'Escape', action: 'Dismisses the listbox popup without changing the selected value.' },
  ]}
/>

### Screen readers and ARIA

- **WAI-ARIA Combobox pattern**: The `<ComboboxInput>` acts as `role="combobox"` linked to the floating `<ComboboxContent>` which acts as `role="listbox"`.
- **`aria-activedescendant`**: Updated dynamically as keyboard arrows cycle highlighted items so screen readers announce each option without shifting native DOM focus from the text input.

## Guidelines

<DoDont>
  <Do>
    Provide an informative `<ComboboxEmpty>` state informing the user when no search results match.
  </Do>
  <Dont>
    Never show an empty, blank floating container when a search yields zero matches.
  </Dont>
</DoDont>

<DoDont>
  <Do>
    Use debounced asynchronous fetching when searching massive datasets over the network.
  </Do>
  <Dont>
    Never trigger an unthrottled HTTP request on every individual keystroke.
  </Dont>
</DoDont>

## API reference

<ApiTable
  components={[
    'Combobox',
    'ComboboxInput',
    'ComboboxContent',
    'ComboboxList',
    'ComboboxItem',
    'ComboboxEmpty',
    'ComboboxGroup',
    'ComboboxGroupLabel',
    'ComboboxSeparator',
  ]}
  baseUi="combobox"
/>

## Related

- [SearchableSelect](/ui/docs/components/forms/searchable-select) — Filterable dropdown menu for medium option lists.
- [Select](/ui/docs/components/forms/select) — Standard dropdown select for short, static option lists.
- [TagInput](/ui/docs/components/forms/tag-input) — Multi-tag entry and keyword selection.

## Date Picker (https://innostes.com/ui/docs/components/forms/date-picker)

DatePicker and DateRangePicker with built-in presets, min/max bounds, clearing triggers, and standard YYYY-MM-DD form submissions.

<ComponentPreview name="forms/date-picker/basic" />

## Import

```tsx
import {
  DatePicker,
  DateRangePicker,
  defaultDateRangePresets,
  type DateRange,
  type DateRangePreset,
} from '@innostes/ui';
```

## When to use

Use `DatePicker` or `DateRangePicker` when users need to select dates within forms, query bars, or filter headers without taking up permanent layout space:

- Setting invoice due dates, quotation validity periods, or purchase order delivery dates.
- Selecting custom reporting intervals or quick presets (such as "Last 30 days" or "This month") in financial analytics.
- Capturing personal dates like date of birth using year/month dropdown navigation.

When choosing between date components:
- Use [Calendar](/ui/docs/components/forms/calendar) directly when you want the month grid permanently visible inline on the page (such as a resource booking calendar or dispatch dashboard).
- Use `DatePicker` for selecting an isolated point in time (e.g. `dueDate`).
- Use `DateRangePicker` when querying date spans bounded by start and end dates.
- Use [Input](/ui/docs/components/forms/input) with `type="date"` if minimal JavaScript bundle size on legacy mobile browsers takes precedence over styling consistency.

## Examples

### Basic date picker

Render `DatePicker` with an accessible label or `aria-label`. Use `value` and `onValueChange` for controlled state.

```tsx
'use client';

import { useState } from 'react';
import { DatePicker, Label } from '@innostes/ui';

export function InvoiceDueDate() {
  const [dueDate, setDueDate] = useState<Date | null>(new Date());

  return (
    <div className="flex flex-col gap-2">
      <Label htmlFor="invoice-due">Payment due date</Label>
      <DatePicker
        id="invoice-due"
        name="dueDate"
        value={dueDate}
        onValueChange={setDueDate}
      />
    </div>
  );
}
```

### Date formatting and locale

The trigger formats dates using `Intl.DateTimeFormat` with `dateStyle: 'medium'` by default. You can supply custom `Intl.DateTimeFormatOptions` or a custom formatting function via the `format` prop. Pass `locale` to ensure month and day names correspond to the user's regional dialect.

```tsx
import { DatePicker } from '@innostes/ui';

export function FormattedDatePicker() {
  return (
    <DatePicker
      locale="en-IN"
      format={{ day: '2-digit', month: 'short', year: 'numeric' }}
      aria-label="Voucher date"
    />
  );
}
```

### Date constraints and disabled days

Bound selectable dates using `min` and `max`. Use `isDateDisabled` to disable specific dates such as regional holidays or non-working days.

```tsx
import { DatePicker } from '@innostes/ui';

const isSunday = (date: Date) => date.getDay() === 0;

export function DeliverySlotPicker() {
  return (
    <DatePicker
      min={new Date()}
      isDateDisabled={isSunday}
      placeholder="Select working day"
      aria-label="Delivery slot"
    />
  );
}
```

### Month and year dropdown navigation

Set `captionLayout="dropdown"` to display dropdown selectors for year and month inside the popover calendar. This is ideal for historical dates such as employee date of birth or company incorporation.

```tsx
import { DatePicker } from '@innostes/ui';

export function DateOfBirthPicker() {
  return (
    <DatePicker
      captionLayout="dropdown"
      fromYear={1950}
      toYear={2010}
      placeholder="Select date of birth"
      aria-label="Date of birth"
    />
  );
}
```

### Date range picker with presets

`DateRangePicker` renders a popover with dual-month navigation alongside quick preset selections (e.g., "Today", "Last 7 days", "Last 30 days", "This month"). The `onValueChange` callback triggers when both `from` and `to` dates are chosen, or immediately when a preset button is clicked.

```tsx
'use client';

import { useState } from 'react';
import { DateRangePicker, type DateRange } from '@innostes/ui';

export function TaxPeriodFilter() {
  const [period, setPeriod] = useState<DateRange>({
    from: new Date(2026, 3, 1),
    to: new Date(2026, 3, 30),
  });

  return (
    <DateRangePicker
      value={period}
      onValueChange={setPeriod}
      startName="startDate"
      endName="endDate"
      aria-label="GST tax period"
    />
  );
}
```

You can define custom presets or pass an empty array (`presets={[]}`) to remove the preset column:

```tsx
import { DateRangePicker, defaultDateRangePresets } from '@innostes/ui';

const fiscalPresets = [
  {
    label: 'Q1 (Apr–Jun)',
    range: () => ({ from: new Date(2026, 3, 1), to: new Date(2026, 5, 30) }),
  },
  ...defaultDateRangePresets,
];

export function CustomPresetsDemo() {
  return <DateRangePicker presets={fiscalPresets} aria-label="Fiscal period" />;
}
```

### Form integration and submission

`DatePicker` renders a hidden `<input type="hidden">` with the chosen date formatted as `YYYY-MM-DD` under the given `name` prop. `DateRangePicker` accepts `startName` and `endName` to submit both dates in standard HTML forms and server actions.

```tsx
import { DatePicker, Field, FieldLabel, FieldError } from '@innostes/ui';

export function FormDatePickerExample() {
  return (
    <form action="/api/v1/invoices" method="POST">
      <Field>
        <FieldLabel htmlFor="due-date">Invoice due date</FieldLabel>
        <DatePicker id="due-date" name="dueDate" required />
        <FieldError />
      </Field>
    </form>
  );
}
```

## Accessibility

`DatePicker` and `DateRangePicker` follow WAI-ARIA combobox and popover dialog specifications.

### Keyboard navigation

<KeyboardTable
  entries={[
    { key: 'Enter / Space', action: 'Opens the calendar popover when focused on the trigger button.' },
    { key: 'Down Arrow', action: 'Opens the calendar popover and shifts keyboard focus to the calendar grid.' },
    { key: 'Escape', action: 'Closes the popover calendar and restores focus to the trigger button.' },
    { key: 'Tab', action: 'Navigates focus within the popover between the calendar grid, presets, and month controls.' },
  ]}
/>

### Screen readers

- The trigger element is an accessible button rendered with `aria-haspopup="dialog"`.
- When opened, focus moves into the calendar grid, which announces the currently focused day with day of week, day number, month, and year.
- Selected dates are announced with `aria-selected="true"`.
- The clear button includes a localized `aria-label` ("Clear date" by default).

## Guidelines

<DoDont
  do={{
    description: 'Provide an explicit label using FieldLabel or an aria-label attribute so screen reader users understand what date is requested.',
    code: `<Label htmlFor="dispatch">Dispatch date</Label>\n<DatePicker id="dispatch" name="dispatchDate" />`,
  }}
  dont={{
    description: 'Do not rely solely on placeholder text as a field label; placeholders vanish once a date is picked.',
    code: `<DatePicker placeholder="Dispatch date" />`,
  }}
/>

<DoDont
  do={{
    description: 'Specify startName and endName on DateRangePicker so HTML form submissions submit cleanly separated ISO dates without extra parsing.',
    code: `<DateRangePicker startName="startDate" endName="endDate" />`,
  }}
  dont={{
    description: 'Do not parse a composite string manually on the server when separate hidden inputs are already provided.',
    code: `// Avoid manual string splitting of "01/04/2026 - 30/04/2026"`,
  }}
/>

## API reference

<ApiTable components={['DatePicker', 'DateRangePicker']} baseUi="popover" />

## Related

- [Calendar](/ui/docs/components/forms/calendar) — Inline calendar month grid for dashboards and date visualization.
- [Field](/ui/docs/components/forms/field) — Form field container with label, description, and error messaging.
- [Input](/ui/docs/components/forms/input) — Standard text, numeric, and native date inputs.

## Field and Form (https://innostes.com/ui/docs/components/forms/field)

Accessible form container linking labels, descriptions, and errors with native constraint validation and server error mapping.

`Field` and `Form` provide the foundational scaffolding for all enterprise forms in `@innostes/ui`. Built on Base UI's field primitive, `Field` automatically links labels to controls via `htmlFor`, connects descriptive notes and error messages via `aria-describedby`, and manages `aria-invalid` without manual ID wiring.

<ComponentPreview name="forms/field/basic" />

## Import

```tsx
import {
  Field,
  FieldLabel,
  FieldDescription,
  FieldError,
  FieldItem,
  Fieldset,
  FieldsetLegend,
  Form,
  FormActions,
  FormGrid,
  FormSection,
} from '@innostes/ui';
```

## When to use

- **Use Field** around any input, select, textarea, or checkbox to automatically manage accessible names, helper text, and validation feedback.
- **Use Form** to coordinate form submission, capture values as keyed objects, map server validation errors, and focus the first invalid control automatically.
- **Use FormGrid and FormSection** to arrange complex ERP forms into structured, responsive multi-column layouts.

## Examples

### Purchase order header

A realistic ERP purchase order header combining `Form`, `FormGrid`, `Field`, `Select`, `Input`, and `FormActions`:

<ComponentPreview name="forms/field/purchase-order-header" />

### Native constraint validation

`Field` integrates with standard browser HTML5 constraint validation attributes (`required`, `minLength`, `pattern`, `min`, `max`):

```tsx
<Field name="email">
  <FieldLabel required>Work email</FieldLabel>
  <Input type="email" required />
  <FieldError match="valueMissing">Email address is required.</FieldError>
  <FieldError match="typeMismatch">Enter a valid email address.</FieldError>
</Field>
```

### Custom and asynchronous validation

Supply a custom validator function via the `validate` prop on `Field`. The function receives the control value and returns an error message string or `null`:

```tsx
<Field
  name="poNumber"
  validate={async (value) => {
    if (!value) return 'PO number is required';
    const exists = await checkPoExistsOnServer(String(value));
    return exists ? 'This purchase order number already exists.' : null;
  }}
>
  <FieldLabel required>PO number</FieldLabel>
  <Input placeholder="PO-2026-0000" />
  <FieldError match="customError" />
</Field>
```

### Server errors mapped to fields

When a backend API rejects a submission, pass the returned error record to `Form`'s `errors` prop. Each error maps automatically to the matching `<FieldError>` child:

<ComponentPreview name="forms/field/form" />

### Validation timing and focus management

By default, validation runs when the form is submitted (`validationMode="onSubmit"`). You can configure `validationMode` on individual fields or across the entire `Form`:

- `onSubmit`: Validates only upon form submission (avoids premature nagging).
- `onBlur`: Validates when the user tabs out of the input.
- `onChange`: Re-validates immediately on keystroke once the field is dirty.

When a submission fails validation, `Form` automatically moves keyboard focus to the **first invalid field** in DOM order, allowing keyboard and screen-reader users to remediate mistakes immediately.

## Accessibility

### Keyboard navigation

<KeyboardTable
  rows={[
    { key: 'Tab', action: 'Moves focus sequentially across interactive controls inside the form.' },
    { key: 'Enter', action: 'Submits the form when focused inside a single-line input field.' },
    { key: 'Escape', action: 'Dismisses active select dropdowns or combobox popups without closing the form.' },
  ]}
/>

### Screen readers and ARIA

- **Automatic `aria-describedby`**: `Field` computes unique internal IDs and sets `aria-describedby` pointing to both `<FieldDescription>` and `<FieldError>`.
- **`aria-invalid`**: Automatically set to `true` on the enclosed input whenever validation fails.
- **Live region error announcements**: `<FieldError>` emits errors in an ARIA live region so screen readers announce corrections without requiring navigation away from the current field.

## Guidelines

<DoDont>
  <Do>
    Always wrap interactive form inputs inside a `<Field>` with a visible `<FieldLabel>` for sustained accessibility.
  </Do>
  <Dont>
    Never rely on input `placeholder` text as a substitute for a visible `<FieldLabel>`.
  </Dont>
</DoDont>

<DoDont>
  <Do>
    Write specific, constructive error messages explaining how to resolve the issue (e.g. "Enter an 8-character GSTIN number").
  </Do>
  <Dont>
    Never emit vague errors such as "Invalid input" or "Field error".
  </Dont>
</DoDont>

## API reference

<ApiTable
  components={[
    'Field',
    'FieldLabel',
    'FieldDescription',
    'FieldError',
    'FieldItem',
    'Fieldset',
    'FieldsetLegend',
    'Form',
    'FormActions',
    'FormGrid',
    'FormSection',
  ]}
  baseUi="field"
/>

- [Input](/ui/docs/components/forms/input) — Single-line text input primitives.
- [Select](/ui/docs/components/forms/select) — Dropdown menu selection.
- [FormLayout](/ui/docs/components/layout/form-layout) — High-level multi-step form layout container.
