## Navigation (https://innostes.com/ui/docs/components/navigation/index)

Structures and controls that guide operators through multi-step journeys and hierarchical data.

import { CategoryGrid } from '@/components/docs/category-grid';

# Navigation

Navigation components establish information architecture and wayfinding across Northwind Traders Pvt Ltd's ERP modules. They provide predictable, keyboard-accessible paths through complex inventory hierarchies, multi-stage procurement flows, and paginated records.

## Components

<CategoryGrid category="components/navigation" />

## Usage guidelines

- **Wayfinding hierarchy**: Combine `Breadcrumb` for relational hierarchy, `Tabs` for alternate views of an entity, and `Stepper` for sequential multi-step wizards.
- **Keyboard navigation**: Tab strips support Left/Right arrow keys for roving focus. Accordions support Up/Down arrow navigation.
- **RTL awareness**: All navigation elements honour document directionality (`dir="rtl"`) with logical margin and icon rotation.

---

## Pagination (https://innostes.com/ui/docs/components/navigation/pagination)

Controlled, translatable, with a stable width as you page.

<ComponentPreview name="navigation/pagination/basic" />

## Import

```tsx
import { Pagination, getPaginationRange } from '@innostes/ui';
```

## Usage

```tsx
const [page, setPage] = useState(1);

<Pagination page={page} pageCount={Math.ceil(total / pageSize)} onPageChange={setPage} />
```

- The number of buttons stays the same as you move, so the controls don't jump under the pointer.
- `labels` translates "Previous", "Next" and the page names.

## Custom pagination UI

`getPaginationRange` returns the items to show (numbers and ellipses), so you can build any layout
on the same logic. It has no React code, so it also works on the server.

```ts
getPaginationRange({ page: 6, pageCount: 20 });
// → [1, 'ellipsis-start', 5, 6, 7, 'ellipsis-end', 20]
```

## Accessibility

- `<nav aria-label="Pagination">`; the current page has `aria-current="page"`; every button is labelled.

## API Reference

<ApiTable components={['Pagination']} />

---

## Stepper (https://innostes.com/ui/docs/components/navigation/stepper)

Horizontal or vertical, with descriptions, error states and clickable completed steps.

<ComponentPreview name="navigation/stepper/basic" />

## Import

```tsx
import { Stepper, type StepperStep } from '@innostes/ui';
```

## Usage

```tsx
const [step, setStep] = useState(0);

<Stepper steps={steps} currentStep={step} onStepClick={setStep} />
```

- Steps before `currentStep` are complete. Set `status: 'error'` on a step to flag a problem.
- With `onStepClick`, completed steps become buttons, so users can go back but not skip ahead.
- `labelPlacement="end"` puts titles next to the markers for a more compact horizontal stepper.

## Vertical

For order tracking, import jobs and long flows:

<ComponentPreview name="navigation/stepper/vertical" />

## Accessibility

- A `<nav aria-label="Progress">` with an ordered list; the current step has `aria-current="step"`.
- Completed and failed steps are announced ("completed", "has errors"), not shown by colour only.

See the [Setup Wizard example](/ui/docs/examples/setup-wizard) for a full flow.

Underline and pill styles with an animated indicator, horizontal or vertical.

```tsx
<Tabs defaultValue="overview">

    <TabsTab value="overview">Overview</TabsTab>
```

## Alert Dialog (https://innostes.com/ui/docs/components/overlays/alert-dialog)

A dialog that can't be dismissed by clicking outside; the user must choose.

```tsx
import {
```

## Writing good confirmations

- Title asks the question: "Delete Acme Corp?", not "Are you sure?".
- Description states the consequence: what's lost, and whether it can be undone.
- The confirm button repeats the action ("Delete customer"), not "OK".

## Accessibility

- `role="alertdialog"`, labelled by the title and described by the description.
- Focus starts inside the dialog; Escape cancels.

## Command Palette (https://innostes.com/ui/docs/components/overlays/command-palette)

A global command palette triggered by a keyboard shortcut (e.g. ⌘K) to quickly navigate and execute actions across the application.

<ComponentPreview name="overlays/command-palette/basic" align="start" className="p-4 sm:p-4" />

## Import

```tsx
import { CommandPalette, CommandItem, CommandGroup } from '@innostes/ui';
```

## Usage

The `CommandPalette` component is a global, floating search overlay designed to help users quickly find pages or perform actions. It includes built-in keyboard shortcut handling and accessible listbox navigation.

Pass an array of grouped items using the `groups` prop. Each item must specify an `id`, `label`, and an `onSelect` callback.

```tsx
function App() {
  const groups = [
    {
      heading: 'Pages',
      items: [
        {
          id: 'orders',
          label: 'Orders',
          icon: <CartIcon />,
          onSelect: () => router.push('/orders')
        },
        // ...
      ]
    },
    {
      heading: 'Actions',
      items: [
        {
          id: 'new-invoice',
          label: 'Create invoice',
          shortcut: 'C I',
          onSelect: createInvoice
        },
        // ...
      ]
    },
  ];

  return <CommandPalette groups={groups} />;
}
```

### Keyboard Shortcuts

By default, the command palette listens for `Ctrl + K` or `⌘ + K` to open. You can change this behavior by setting the `hotkey` prop to a different character, or pass `null` to disable the built-in shortcut and manage opening state yourself.

### Custom Filtering

The component automatically filters items based on a case- and accent-insensitive search against the item's `label`, `description`, and `keywords`.

If you need a more advanced filtering algorithm, you can provide a custom `filter` function:

```tsx
<CommandPalette
  groups={groups}
  filter={(item, query) => customMatch(item.label, query)}
/>
```

### Advanced Styling

You can deeply customize the internal parts of the palette using the `classNames` prop, targeting slots like `popup`, `input`, `list`, `groupHeading`, `item`, `empty`, and `footer`.

## API Reference

<ApiTable components={['CommandPalette']} />

## Dialog (https://innostes.com/ui/docs/components/overlays/dialog)

Focus trap, Escape and outside-click to close, nested dialogs, and five sizes.

<ComponentPreview name="overlays/dialog/basic" />

## Import

```tsx
import {
  Dialog,
  DialogTrigger,
  DialogContent,
  DialogHeader,
  DialogTitle,
  DialogDescription,
  DialogFooter,
  DialogClose,
} from '@innostes/ui';
```

## Anatomy

```tsx
<Dialog>
  <DialogTrigger />
  <DialogContent>
    <DialogHeader>
      <DialogTitle />
      <DialogDescription />
    </DialogHeader>
    {/* content */}
    <DialogFooter>
      <DialogClose />
    </DialogFooter>
  </DialogContent>
</Dialog>
```

## Usage

- Use `render` to make the trigger and close buttons our `Button`:
  `<DialogTrigger render={<Button />}>Edit</DialogTrigger>`.
- Control it with `open` / `onOpenChange` to close after an async save (see the demo).
- `size` on `DialogContent`: `sm`, `md` (default), `lg`, `xl`, `full`.
- Set `showCloseButton={false}` to hide the × button.

Use a dialog for short, focused tasks. For larger forms next to the content, a
[Sheet](/ui/docs/components/overlays/sheet) keeps more context visible. To confirm destructive
actions, use [Alert Dialog](/ui/docs/components/overlays/alert-dialog).

## Accessibility

- Focus moves into the dialog on open and back to the trigger on close; Tab stays inside.
- Labelled by `DialogTitle` and described by `DialogDescription`. Always include a title.

## Dropdown Menu (https://innostes.com/ui/docs/components/overlays/dropdown-menu)

Groups, shortcuts, checkbox and radio items, submenus and destructive actions.

## Import

```tsx
import {
  DropdownMenu,
  DropdownMenuTrigger,
  DropdownMenuContent,
  DropdownMenuItem,
  DropdownMenuLinkItem,
  DropdownMenuCheckboxItem,

  DropdownMenuRadioItem,

  DropdownMenuSeparator,
  DropdownMenuShortcut,
  DropdownMenuSub,
  DropdownMenuSubTrigger,
} from '@innostes/ui';
```

## Row actions

The most common admin pattern: a "⋯" button per table row.

```tsx
<DropdownMenu>
  <DropdownMenuTrigger render={<Button variant="ghost" size="sm" iconOnly aria-label={`Actions for ${order.id}`} />}>
    <MoreHorizontalIcon />
  </DropdownMenuTrigger>
  <DropdownMenuContent align="end">
    <DropdownMenuItem onClick={() => open(order)}>View</DropdownMenuItem>
    <DropdownMenuSeparator />
    <DropdownMenuItem variant="destructive" onClick={() => refund(order)}>Refund</DropdownMenuItem>
  </DropdownMenuContent>
</DropdownMenu>
```

## Submenus

Put a `DropdownMenuSubTrigger` and a `DropdownMenuContent` inside `DropdownMenuSub`.

## Accessibility

- Arrow keys move between items, type-ahead jumps to an item, Enter/Space activates, Escape closes.
- `DropdownMenuShortcut` is a visual hint only; register the keyboard shortcut yourself.

## Overlays (https://innostes.com/ui/docs/components/overlays/index)

Layered interface elements that appear above base page content for focused interactions.

import { CategoryGrid } from '@/components/docs/category-grid';

# Overlays

Overlays present supplementary workflows, context-sensitive details, and decision prompts above the primary page canvas. They enable Northwind Traders operators to complete focused sub-tasks without navigating away from their active workspace.

## Components

<CategoryGrid category="components/overlays" />

## Usage guidelines

- **Modality**: Use `Dialog` or `AlertDialog` when operator confirmation or focused data entry is mandatory before proceeding. Use `Sheet` for wide inspection panels and edit drawers.
- **Focus management**: Overlays automatically trap focus when opened, restore focus to the triggering element upon dismissal, and close on Escape key navigation.
- **Progressive disclosure**: Reserve `Tooltip` for non-essential keyboard hints and iconography descriptions. Use `Popover` for rich interactive menus and filters.

## Tooltip (https://innostes.com/ui/docs/components/overlays/tooltip)

Names icon buttons and shows shortcuts. Shared delay across a toolbar.

<ComponentPreview name="overlays/tooltip/basic" />

## Import

```tsx
import { Tooltip, TooltipTrigger, TooltipContent, TooltipProvider } from '@innostes/ui';
```

## Usage

```tsx
<Tooltip>
  <TooltipTrigger render={<Button iconOnly variant="ghost" aria-label="Archive" />}>
    <ArchiveIcon />
  </TooltipTrigger>
  <TooltipContent>Archive</TooltipContent>
</Tooltip>
```

Wrap your app in `TooltipProvider` once. After the first tooltip opens, moving to the next trigger
shows it instantly, which makes toolbars feel fast.

## Accessibility

- Opens on hover and keyboard focus; Escape closes it.
- Tooltips are not reachable on touch devices and are skipped by some screen readers. The trigger
  still needs its own `aria-label`, and tooltips must never hold essential information.

## Colour (https://innostes.com/ui/docs/foundations/colour)

OKLCH semantic palette, contrast tokens, functional roles, and verified WCAG 2.2 AA contrast ratios.

import { ContrastTable } from '@/components/docs/contrast-table';

The `@innostes/ui` colour system is engineered for enterprise ERP operations where clarity, data hierarchy, and visual ergonomics are paramount. Formulated in the **OKLCH colour space**, our palette guarantees perceptual uniformity across shades, ensuring predictable contrast ratios and consistent luminance across light and dark display modes.

## Semantic architecture

Components reference functional colour tokens rather than raw hex codes. Every token represents an operational role:

| Role | Intended application | Primary pairing |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `background` / `foreground` | Root viewport canvas and primary body typography | Default page canvas |
| `card` / `card-foreground` | Contained surfaces, data tables, side panels, and modal windows | Layered elevation |
| `popover` / `popover-foreground` | Transient floating overlays, dropdown menus, and tooltips | Elevated z-index layer |
| `primary` / `primary-foreground` | High-priority interactive triggers, primary form submissions | Brand action |
| `secondary` / `secondary-foreground` | Alternative action triggers, filter chips, and pill toggles | Muted action |
| `muted` / `muted-foreground` | Table column headers, field helper notes, and deactivated fills | Tertiary context |
| `accent` / `accent-foreground` | Highlighted table rows, active navigation items, and list hovers | Interactive feedback |
| `destructive` / `destructive-foreground` | Irreversible operations, voiding invoices, cancellation alerts | Critical risk |
| `success` / `success-foreground` | Approved purchase orders, paid status indicators, successful syncs | Positive confirmation |
| `warning` / `warning-foreground` | Overdue shipments, pending review alerts, stock reorder warnings | Attention required |
| `info` / `info-foreground` | Informational callouts, carrier transit updates, system advisories | Neutral context |

## Accessibility & contrast guarantees

Under WCAG 2.2 Level AA:
- **Normal text** (under 18pt or bold under 14pt) requires a minimum contrast ratio of **4.5:1** against its background.
- **Large text** (18pt+ or bold 14pt+) and graphical user interface components require a minimum contrast ratio of **3.0:1**.

The table below is computed at build time from `packages/ui/tailwind/theme.css` and `packages/ui/tailwind/dark.css`. Every token pairing satisfies the 4.5:1 normal text standard in both light and dark themes:

<ContrastTable />

## Guidelines for colour application

1. **Never convey meaning through colour alone**: When indicating status (e.g. an unpaid invoice or failed dispatch), always pair the semantic colour token with text or an icon (such as an alert triangle or checkmark) so colour-blind operators at Northwind Traders can distinguish states immediately.
2. **Preserve token pairing**: Always use a background token with its corresponding foreground counterpart (e.g. `bg-primary text-primary-foreground` or `bg-destructive text-destructive-foreground`). Never mix mismatched tokens like `text-white` on `bg-warning`.
3. **Reserve destructive for high-consequence operations**: Do not use `destructive` for optional cancel buttons. Reserve red fills for permanent deletions, invoice voiding, or warehouse order cancellations.

---

## Dark Mode (https://innostes.com/ui/docs/foundations/dark-mode)

Implement dark mode across applications using class-based or data-attribute activation, next-themes, and hydration safeguards.

import { Step, Steps } from 'fumadocs-ui/components/steps';
import { Tab, Tabs } from 'fumadocs-ui/components/tabs';

`@innostes/ui` includes native dark mode styling for every component, widget, chart, and modal primitive. Theme switching works without JavaScript state recalculations: toggling an ancestor CSS class or attribute remaps the underlying CSS custom properties instantly.

## How to enable dark mode

Import the dark stylesheet in your application CSS entry point directly after the base tokens:

```css title="app/globals.css"
@import "tailwindcss";
@import "@innostes/ui/tailwind.css";
@import "@innostes/ui/dark.css";
```

`@innostes/ui/dark.css` registers rules targeting either the `.dark` class or the `[data-theme='dark']` attribute on any ancestor (typically the root `<html>` element):

```css
/* Activated automatically by dark.css */
.dark,
[data-theme='dark'] {
  color-scheme: dark;
  --color-background: oklch(14.1% 0.005 285.823);
  --color-foreground: oklch(98.5% 0 0);
  /* Remaining semantic token remaps */
}
```

## Strategy: Class vs Data-Attribute

`@innostes/ui` supports both conventions identically:

| Strategy | Activation selector | Best suited for |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Class strategy** (recommended) | `<html class="dark">` | Standard Tailwind CSS workflows and `next-themes` default mode |
| **Data attribute strategy** | `<html data-theme="dark">` | Multi-theme applications (e.g. `data-theme="high-contrast"`) |

## Integration with next-themes

In Next.js applications, use `next-themes` to manage theme preference, system synchronization, and local storage persistence.

```tsx title="components/theme-provider.tsx"
'use client';

import * as React from 'react';
import { ThemeProvider as NextThemesProvider } from 'next-themes';

export function ThemeProvider({
  children,
  ...props
}: React.ComponentProps<typeof NextThemesProvider>) {
  return (
    <NextThemesProvider
      attribute="class"
      defaultTheme="system"
      enableSystem
      disableTransitionOnChange
      {...props}
    >
      {children}
    </NextThemesProvider>
  );
}
```

## Avoiding flash of the wrong theme

A common issue in server-rendered applications is Flash of Unstyled Theme (FOUT), where a user with a dark mode preference briefly sees a blinding white screen before client hydration.

To prevent FOUT:

1. **Add `suppressHydrationWarning`**: Always add this prop to the `<html>` tag in your root layout. This tells React to ignore differences between the server-rendered HTML and client-injected theme classes.
2. **Use `disableTransitionOnChange`**: When switching themes, temporarily disable CSS transitions to prevent color property interpolation flickers across buttons and borders.
3. **Vanilla / Vite blocking script**: For client-side Single Page Applications without `next-themes`, place a tiny synchronous script inside the `<head>` tag of `index.html`:

```html title="index.html"
<head>
  <script>
    (function() {
      const theme = localStorage.getItem('theme');
      const prefersDark = window.matchMedia('(prefers-color-scheme: dark)').matches;
      if (theme === 'dark' || (!theme && prefersDark)) {
        document.documentElement.classList.add('dark');
      }
    })();
  </script>
</head>
```

## How to test dark mode

### Unit testing with Vitest and Testing Library

Verify that components respond correctly when the dark mode class is applied to the container:

```tsx title="src/components/theme.test.tsx"
import { render, screen } from '@testing-library/react';
import { describe, it, expect, beforeEach, afterEach } from 'vitest';
import { Button } from '@innostes/ui';

describe('Dark mode rendering', () => {
  beforeEach(() => {
    document.documentElement.classList.add('dark');
  });

  afterEach(() => {
    document.documentElement.classList.remove('dark');
  });

  it('renders primary button under dark theme class', () => {
    render(<Button variant="primary">Approve PO</Button>);
    const button = screen.getByRole('button', { name: 'Approve PO' });
    expect(button).toBeInTheDocument();
    expect(document.documentElement).toHaveClass('dark');
  });
});
```

### End-to-end testing with Playwright

Test dark theme visual rendering and token contrast using Playwright's color scheme emulation:

```ts title="tests/theme.spec.ts"
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test.describe('Dark theme operations portal', () => {
  test.use({ colorScheme: 'dark' });

  test('displays dark background and correct token contrast', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/dashboard');
    const html = page.locator('html');
    await expect(html).toHaveClass(/dark/);

    const body = page.locator('body');
    await expect(body).toHaveCSS('background-color', 'rgb(9, 9, 11)');
  });
});
```

---

## Icons (https://innostes.com/ui/docs/foundations/icons)

Iconography standards, Lucide React integration, sizing rules inside components, and accessibility requirements.

`@innostes/ui` standardises on [`lucide-react`](https://lucide.dev) for interface iconography. Lucide icons provide consistent 24px bounding boxes, balanced optical weights (2px default stroke), and clean geometric curves that pair naturally with the typography scale.

## Recommended package

Install `lucide-react` in your project:

```bash
pnpm add lucide-react
```

## Sizing standards inside components

Icons inside `@innostes/ui` primitives should match the surrounding font metrics. Use Tailwind's `size-*` utility classes to constrain both width and height simultaneously:

| Component context | Recommended size | Tailwind utility | Example pairing |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Badges, compact chips, table tags | 14px × 14px | `size-3.5` | `<CheckCircle2 className="size-3.5 me-1" />` |
| Standard buttons (`size="md"`), form inputs | 16px × 16px | `size-4` | `<Search className="size-4 me-1.5" />` |
| Large buttons (`size="lg"`), dialog headers | 20px × 20px | `size-5` | `<Download className="size-5 me-2" />` |
| Application rail items, widget header icons | 24px × 24px | `size-6` | `<Building2 className="size-6 text-primary" />` |

## Optical alignment and RTL spacing

To preserve bidirectional text support (Left-to-Right and Right-to-Left), never use physical margin utilities like `mr-*` or `ml-*` on icons. Use CSS logical inline margins:

```tsx
// Leading icon: Margin inline end
<Button variant="primary">
  <CheckCircle2 className="size-4 me-1.5" />
  <span>Approve purchase order</span>
</Button>

// Trailing icon: Margin inline start
<Button variant="outline">
  <span>Review delivery schedule</span>
  <ChevronRight className="size-4 ms-1.5" />
</Button>
```

In Left-to-Right layouts, `me-1.5` outputs `margin-right: 0.375rem`. In Right-to-Left layouts (e.g. Arabic or Hebrew), it automatically flips to `margin-left: 0.375rem`.

## Accessibility requirements

### Decorative icons

When an icon accompanies descriptive text (such as "Download invoice PDF" next to a file icon), the icon is purely decorative. Lucide React components include `aria-hidden="true"` by default. Ensure custom SVGs also declare `aria-hidden="true"` so screen readers do not announce redundant symbols:

```tsx
// Correct: Screen reader announces only "Download invoice"
<Button variant="outline">
  <FileDown className="size-4 me-1.5" aria-hidden="true" />
  <span>Download invoice</span>
</Button>
```

### Icon-only buttons

When rendering a button that contains only an icon (such as a close cross, edit pencil, or notification bell), assistive technologies cannot infer the action from visual glyphs.

You **must** provide a descriptive `aria-label` or an accessible visually hidden label:

```tsx
// Required: aria-label clarifies the action for screen-reader users
<Button
  variant="ghost"
  size="icon"
  aria-label="Delete line item 14 from purchase order"
  onClick={handleDelete}
>
  <Trash2 className="size-4 text-destructive" />
</Button>
```

Alternatively, wrap tooltip components around icon buttons to provide both visual hovering cues and assistive hints:

```tsx
<Tooltip>
  <TooltipTrigger render={
    <Button variant="ghost" size="icon" aria-label="Export ledger to Excel">
      <FileSpreadsheet className="size-4" />
    </Button>
  } />
  <TooltipContent>Export ledger to Excel (.xlsx)</TooltipContent>
</Tooltip>
```

---

## Motion (https://innostes.com/ui/docs/foundations/motion)

Transition durations, easing curves, and prefers-reduced-motion accessibility standards.

Motion in `@innostes/ui` is functional, understated, and swift. Animation serves exclusively to orient operators during spatial state transitions—such as expanding accordion panels, opening dialog overlays, sliding drawers, and displaying toast notifications.

In high-density ERP and logistics environments, excessive decorative animation introduces cognitive friction. Every motion token is bounded by strict duration ceilings.

## Duration scale

The design system standardises on four deterministic duration tokens:

| Token / Utility | Milliseconds | Recommended application |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `duration-75` | 75ms | Micro-feedback (button active depress, toggle knob shift) |
| `duration-150` | 150ms | Tooltip reveals, dropdown menu item hover fills, checkbox checkmarks |
| `duration-200` | 200ms | Sidebar width collapse (`Sidebar`), dropdown popup scale entrances |
| `duration-300` | 300ms | Modal dialog entrances (`Dialog`), sheet drawer slide-ins (`Sheet`), accordion panel reveal |

Transitions exceeding 300ms are strictly avoided to ensure interface responsiveness across operational terminals at Northwind Traders.

## Easing curves

Natural physics curves govern component transitions:

```css
/* Entrances: Natural decelerate curve (swift entry, gentle settle) */
--ease-out: cubic-bezier(0, 0, 0.2, 1);

/* Standard transitions: Smooth symmetric curve */
--ease-in-out: cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 0.2, 1);

/* Exits and dismissals: Quick accelerate curve */
--ease-in: cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 1, 1);
```

## Reduced-motion behaviour

For operators with vestibular motion disorders or sensory sensitivities, continuous animation or sudden spatial displacement can cause dizziness and discomfort.

`@innostes/ui` respects the user's `prefers-reduced-motion` operating system setting across all components:

- **Skeleton**: Replaces continuous pulsing (`animate-pulse`) with a static muted background fill via `motion-reduce:animate-none`.
- **Sidebar**: Collapses width instantly without transition tweening using `motion-reduce:transition-none`.
- **Progress**: Disables continuous indeterminate bar sweeps via `motion-reduce:data-indeterminate:animate-none`.
- **Dialogs & Sheets**: Replaces slide-and-scale physics with an instantaneous opacity fade.

### Testing reduced motion

To verify reduced-motion compliance in development:

1. Open Chrome DevTools or Firefox Developer Tools.
2. Open the Rendering drawer (`Ctrl+Shift+P` / `Cmd+Shift+P` -> type "Rendering").
3. Set **Emulate CSS media feature prefers-reduced-motion** to `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`.
4. Trigger sidebars, dialogs, and progress bars: confirm that physical movement is replaced with instantaneous state changes.

---

## Spacing and Layout (https://innostes.com/ui/docs/foundations/spacing)

4px base spatial rhythm, density modes, container queries, and responsive layout primitives.

`@innostes/ui` constructs layouts using a **4-pixel base grid**. Consistent spatial intervals eliminate visual clutter, guarantee optical balance, and establish clear structural hierarchies across complex ERP workflows.

## The 4px spacing scale

All margin, padding, gap, and component dimension values increment in multiples of 4 pixels:

| Token / Class | Pixels | Rem equivalent | Primary usage |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `0.5` | 2px | 0.125rem | Hairline borders, sub-pixel alignment offsets |
| `1` | 4px | 0.25rem | Gap between button icons and text labels, inline badge padding |
| `1.5` | 6px | 0.375rem | Compact menu item vertical padding |
| `2` | 8px | 0.5rem | Button vertical padding (small), form label margins |
| `2.5` | 10px | 0.625rem | Standard input vertical padding |
| `3` | 12px | 0.75rem | Standard button horizontal padding, table cell vertical padding |
| `4` | 16px | 1.0rem | Standard card internal padding, dialog gutters, component gaps |
| `6` | 24px | 1.5rem | Page section margins, large modal gutters |
| `8` | 32px | 2.0rem | Dashboard grid column gaps, page header margins |
| `12` | 48px | 3.0rem | Top-level view gutters on desktop screens |

## Density modes

Enterprise ERP operators frequently switch between high-density review screens (e.g. reviewing 500 purchase order lines) and standard operational forms. `@innostes/ui` supports density adaptation across data display and form primitives:

| Density mode | Table row height | Input height | Button padding | Recommended context |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Compact** | 32px | 32px (`size="sm"`) | `py-1 px-2.5` | Data audit grids, split-pane inspection panels |
| **Default** | 44px | 40px (`size="md"`) | `py-2 px-3.5` | Standard operations forms, purchase order authoring |
| **Comfortable** | 56px | 48px (`size="lg"`) | `py-3 px-5` | Touch-screen warehouse terminals, welcome wizards |

```tsx title="Example: Compact vs Default Table Rows"
// Compact data grid for invoice auditing
<Table className="text-xs">
  <TableRow className="h-8">
    <TableCell className="py-1 px-2.5 font-mono">INV-8901</TableCell>
    <TableCell className="py-1 px-2.5">₹45,000.00</TableCell>
  </TableRow>
</Table>
```

## Container queries

In modular dashboards, components are frequently placed into variable-width containers (such as resizable `SplitPane` panels, collapsing sidebars, or multi-column card grids). Relying on viewport media queries (`@media (min-width: ...)`) causes components to render poorly when housed inside a narrow panel on a wide screen.

`@innostes/ui` leverages CSS Container Queries (`@container`) across composite widgets:

```tsx title="components/order-summary-card.tsx"
export function OrderSummaryCard() {
  return (
    // Declare container context on wrapper
    <div className="@container rounded-xl border border-border bg-card p-4">
      {/* Stack vertically in narrow slots, switch to row when container exceeds 380px */}
      <div className="flex flex-col @[380px]:flex-row @[380px]:items-center @[380px]:justify-between gap-3">
        <div>
          <span className="text-xs text-muted-foreground">Order PO-2026-0881</span>
          <div className="text-lg font-semibold text-foreground">₹1,45,280.00</div>
        </div>
        <button className="w-full @[380px]:w-auto text-xs py-1.5 px-3 rounded bg-primary text-primary-foreground">
          View details
        </button>
      </div>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Core layout primitives

| Component | Responsibility | Documentation link |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `Sidebar` | Multi-level collapsible navigation panel supporting fixed, floating, and mini rail modes | [Sidebar docs](/ui/docs/components/layout/sidebar) |
| `AppRail` | Ultra-compact vertical icon rail for switching top-level enterprise modules | [App Rail docs](/ui/docs/components/layout/app-rail) |
| `TopBar` | Global application header with search, notifications, tenant switcher, and user menu | [Top Bar docs](/ui/docs/components/layout/top-bar) |
| `PageHeader` | Standardised title banner with breadcrumbs, descriptions, and action triggers | [Page Header docs](/ui/docs/components/layout/page-header) |
| `SplitPane` | Resizable multi-column workspace with keyboard collapse and state persistence | [Split Pane docs](/ui/docs/components/layout/split-pane) |
| `ScrollArea` | Custom cross-browser scrollbar container that preserves keyboard accessibility | [Scroll Area docs](/ui/docs/components/layout/scroll-area) |

## Status legend (https://innostes.com/ui/docs/foundations/status-legend)

Stability tiers and readiness criteria for components in @innostes/ui.

# Status legend

Every component, widget, and chart in `@innostes/ui` carries an explicit status badge reflecting its API stability and production readiness. These statuses establish clear expectations for application developers across Northwind Traders Pvt Ltd.

## Status tiers

### Stable

The component has completed thorough browser QA, unit testing, and accessibility verification. Its public API conforms strictly to Semantic Versioning (SemVer).

- **Breaking changes**: Breaking changes occur only in major version increments (e.g. `1.0.0` to `2.0.0`), accompanied by migration guides and codemods where feasible.
- **Production readiness**: Recommended for all mission-critical production interfaces and customer-facing workflows.
- **Support**: Receives active maintenance, security patches, and forward-compatibility testing across supported React runtimes.

### Beta

The component is functionally complete and usable in production environments, but its API surface may undergo refinements based on enterprise team feedback.

- **Breaking changes**: Breaking modifications may occur in minor version increments (e.g. `0.2.0` to `0.3.0`), with documented migration paths in release notes.
- **Production readiness**: Suitable for early adoption, internal pilot tools, and feature development with active developer oversight.
- **Feedback**: Developers are encouraged to report ergonomics issues and edge cases before the component graduates to Stable.

### Experimental

The component represents an early architectural exploration or prototype. It demonstrates emerging interaction patterns or evaluates new underlying technologies.

- **Breaking changes**: Breaking changes or removal may occur in any release without prior deprecation notices.
- **Production readiness**: Intended strictly for experimentation and design prototyping. Avoid using in core enterprise transactions.

## Graduation criteria

A component graduates from Beta to Stable only when meeting all of the following requirements:

1. **Complete documentation**: Full adherence to the component documentation template, including anatomical breakdown, interactive examples, do/don't guidelines, and keyboard interaction tables.
2. **Automated test coverage**: Unit and integration test suites covering at least 90% statement coverage across all visual variants, states, and accessibility hooks.
3. **Multi-runtime verification**: Verified operational stability across React 19, React 18, and React 17 environments.
4. **Design token conformance**: Full support for both light and dark themes using OKLCH colour tokens and CSS variables.

---

## Typography (https://innostes.com/ui/docs/foundations/typography)

Typography scale, fluid type tokens, font stacks, and tabular numeric rules for enterprise ERP interfaces.

The typographic scale in `@innostes/ui` balances compact information density with prolonged reading ergonomics. Designed for accounting ledgers, purchase order data grids, and inventory consoles at Northwind Traders Pvt Ltd, typography rules prioritise structural alignment and immediate legibility.

## Font families

The design system standardises on two primary font stacks:

| Stack | Font family specification | Intended usage |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `font-sans` | `Inter, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, "Segoe UI", Roboto, sans-serif` | Interface labels, navigation items, dialog titles, and general prose |
| `font-mono` | `ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Monaco, Consolas, "Liberation Mono", monospace` | Monetary figures, invoice identifiers, tracking codes, and code snippets |

## Fluid type tokens

For responsive dashboards that adapt across mobile terminals and widescreen warehouse wall displays, `@innostes/ui` defines responsive fluid type tokens calculated using CSS `clamp()` in `packages/ui/tailwind/theme.css`:

| Utility class | CSS clamp definition | Line height | Recommended application |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `text-display` | `clamp(1.75rem, 1.35rem + 1.6vw, 2.5rem)` | 1.15 | Main hero headers, marketing showcase titles, welcome screen banners |
| `text-heading` | `clamp(1.375rem, 1.2rem + 0.75vw, 1.875rem)` | 1.20 | Page headers (`PageHeader`), modal dialog titles, main section divides |
| `text-subheading` | `clamp(1rem, 0.95rem + 0.2vw, 1.125rem)` | 1.40 | Card titles, subsection dividers, drawer titles |
| `text-metric` | `clamp(1.375rem, 1.15rem + 0.9vw, 1.875rem)` | 1.15 | Key performance indicators (`MetricCard`), total invoice balances |

### Fluid typography example

```tsx
export function WarehouseHeader() {
  return (
    <div className="space-y-1">
      <h1 className="text-heading font-bold text-foreground">
        Whitefield Central Logistics Depot
      </h1>
      <p className="text-subheading text-muted-foreground">
        Active shipment processing and pallet clearance console
      </p>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Static typographic scale

For dense tabular displays, inputs, and form fields where deterministic line height is required for pixel alignment:

| Class | Font size | Line height | Tracking | Primary usage |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `text-xs` | 0.75rem (12px) | 1rem (16px) | Normal | Badge text, helper descriptions, table captions, timestamps |
| `text-sm` | 0.875rem (14px) | 1.25rem (20px) | Normal | Standard enterprise body, form inputs, button labels, grid cells |
| `text-base` | 1.0rem (16px) | 1.5rem (24px) | Normal | Reading prose, long-form documentation, modal body paragraphs |
| `text-lg` | 1.125rem (18px) | 1.75rem (28px) | Tight | Secondary widget titles, summary card headlines |
| `text-xl` | 1.25rem (20px) | 1.75rem (28px) | Tight | Drawer drawer headers, intermediate statistics |
| `text-2xl` | 1.5rem (24px) | 2.0rem (32px) | Tight | Top-level summary banners, dashboard metrics |

## Tabular figures in financial tables

In accounting tables, invoice summaries, and financial reports, non-monospaced numbers cause columns of currency figures to jitter vertically because the digit `1` occupies less horizontal width than `8`.

Always apply `font-mono` or `tabular-nums` when presenting numerical totals or currency values:

```tsx
// Correct: Columns remain strictly aligned across rows
<td className="text-right font-mono text-sm text-foreground">
  ₹1,45,280.00
</td>
```

## Next.js App Router (https://innostes.com/ui/docs/frameworks/nextjs)

Complete integration guide for Next.js App Router, Server Components, dark mode with next-themes, and styling.

import { Step, Steps } from 'fumadocs-ui/components/steps';
import { Tab, Tabs } from 'fumadocs-ui/components/tabs';

`@innostes/ui` is engineered to work directly with Next.js App Router. Interactive primitives ship with `'use client'` directives at their entry boundaries, allowing developers to import them into React Server Components (RSCs) without additional wrappers.

## Architectural boundaries

When developing with Next.js App Router, understand how `@innostes/ui` components interact with the server/client boundary:

1. **Direct RSC composition**: Interactive components such as `Button`, `DataTable`, `Dialog`, and `Tabs` declare `'use client'` internally. You can import and render them directly inside server-rendered `page.tsx` or `layout.tsx` files.
2. **Server-side utilities**: Pure helper functions including `cn()`, `formatDate()`, and variant factories (`buttonVariants()`, `badgeVariants()`) contain no DOM or browser dependencies and execute safely in Server Components, Route Handlers, and Server Actions.
3. **Event handlers & state**: Passing callbacks (such as `onClick`, `onValueChange`, or `onSubmit`) across the server-to-client boundary requires defining that sub-tree inside a client component (`'use client'`).

## Step-by-step setup

<Steps>
<Step>

### Install dependencies

Install `@innostes/ui` alongside `next-themes` and `lucide-react`:

```bash tab="pnpm"
pnpm add @innostes/ui next-themes lucide-react
```

```bash tab="npm"
npm install @innostes/ui next-themes lucide-react
```

```bash tab="yarn"
yarn add @innostes/ui next-themes lucide-react
```

```bash tab="bun"
bun add @innostes/ui next-themes lucide-react
```

</Step>
<Step>

### Configure stylesheet imports

In your Next.js application global stylesheet, import Tailwind CSS followed by the `@innostes/ui` design tokens:

```css title="app/globals.css"
@import "tailwindcss";
@import "@innostes/ui/tailwind.css";
@import "@innostes/ui/dark.css";
```

</Step>
<Step>

### Create the ThemeProvider wrapper

Because `next-themes` requires React context, create a client wrapper component:

```tsx title="components/theme-provider.tsx"
'use client';

import * as React from 'react';
import { ThemeProvider as NextThemesProvider } from 'next-themes';

export function ThemeProvider({
  children,
  ...props
}: React.ComponentProps<typeof NextThemesProvider>) {
  return <NextThemesProvider {...props}>{children}</NextThemesProvider>;
}
```

</Step>
<Step>

### Assemble the root layout

Configure your `app/layout.tsx` with hydration protection, theme switching, and global UI providers:

```tsx title="app/layout.tsx"
import type { Metadata } from 'next';
import { Inter } from 'next/font/google';
import { Toaster, TooltipProvider } from '@innostes/ui';
import { ThemeProvider } from '@/components/theme-provider';
import './globals.css';

const inter = Inter({ subsets: ['latin'] });

export const metadata: Metadata = {
  title: 'Northwind Traders ERP',
  description: 'Operations management portal for Northwind Traders Pvt Ltd',
};

export default function RootLayout({
  children,
}: {
  children: React.ReactNode;
}) {
  return (
    <html lang="en" suppressHydrationWarning>
      <body className={inter.className}>
        <ThemeProvider
          attribute="class"
          defaultTheme="system"
          enableSystem
          disableTransitionOnChange
        >
          <TooltipProvider delayDuration={200}>
            {children}
            <Toaster position="bottom-end" />
          </TooltipProvider>
        </ThemeProvider>
      </body>
    </html>
  );
}
```

> [!NOTE]
> `suppressHydrationWarning` on `<html>` prevents React from reporting mismatches caused by `next-themes` injecting the active theme class (`class="dark"`) prior to client hydration.

</Step>
<Step>

### Build a theme toggle button

Create an accessible theme toggle that switches between light, dark, and system modes:

```tsx title="components/theme-toggle.tsx"
'use client';

import * as React from 'react';
import { useTheme } from 'next-themes';
import { Button } from '@innostes/ui';
import { Moon, Sun } from 'lucide-react';

export function ThemeToggle() {
  const { theme, setTheme } = useTheme();
  const [mounted, setMounted] = React.useState(false);

  React.useEffect(() => {
    setMounted(true);
  }, []);

  if (!mounted) {
    return <Button variant="outline" size="sm" aria-label="Toggle colour theme" disabled />;
  }

  return (
    <Button
      variant="outline"
      size="sm"
      aria-label="Toggle colour theme"
      onClick={() => setTheme(theme === 'dark' ? 'light' : 'dark')}
    >
      {theme === 'dark' ? (
        <Sun className="size-4 me-1.5 text-amber-500" />
      ) : (
        <Moon className="size-4 me-1.5 text-blue-600" />
      )}
      <span>{theme === 'dark' ? 'Light mode' : 'Dark mode'}</span>
    </Button>
  );
}
```

</Step>
<Step>

### Render a Server Component page

Compose library components directly within your server-rendered home page:

```tsx title="app/page.tsx"
import { Button } from '@innostes/ui';
import { ThemeToggle } from '@/components/theme-toggle';
import { ArrowRight, Package } from 'lucide-react';
import Link from 'next/link';

export default async function HomePage() {
  // Server-side data fetching runs safely
  const organisation = 'Northwind Traders Pvt Ltd';
  const openOrdersCount = 42;

  return (
    <main className="min-h-screen p-8 max-w-5xl mx-auto space-y-6">
      <header className="flex items-center justify-between border-b border-border pb-4">
        <div>
          <h1 className="text-2xl font-bold text-foreground">{organisation}</h1>
          <p className="text-sm text-muted-foreground">Bengaluru Distribution Hub</p>
        </div>
        <ThemeToggle />
      </header>

      <section className="rounded-xl border border-border bg-card p-6 shadow-xs space-y-4">
        <div className="flex items-center gap-3">
          <div className="p-2.5 rounded-lg bg-primary/10 text-primary">
            <Package className="size-5" />
          </div>
          <div>
            <h2 className="text-base font-semibold text-foreground">Active Fulfilment Queue</h2>
            <p className="text-xs text-muted-foreground">{openOrdersCount} purchase orders awaiting clearance</p>
          </div>
        </div>

        <div className="pt-2">
          <Button
            variant="primary"
            render={<Link href="/orders" />}
          >
            Review orders
            <ArrowRight className="size-4 ms-1.5" />
          </Button>
        </div>
      </section>
    </main>
  );
}
```

</Step>
</Steps>

## Vite React (https://innostes.com/ui/docs/frameworks/vite)

Complete integration guide for Vite React projects with Tailwind CSS v4, TypeScript, and dark mode.

import { Step, Steps } from 'fumadocs-ui/components/steps';
import { Tab, Tabs } from 'fumadocs-ui/components/tabs';

`@innostes/ui` ships with standard ECMAScript modules (ESM) and precompiled CSS files that integrate directly with Vite React applications.

## Prerequisites

Initialize a standard Vite React TypeScript application if you do not have an existing workspace:

```bash
pnpm create vite northwind-portal --template react-ts
cd northwind-portal
```

## Step-by-step setup

<Steps>
<Step>

### Install dependencies

Install `@innostes/ui` alongside `lucide-react`:

```bash tab="pnpm"
pnpm add @innostes/ui lucide-react
```

```bash tab="npm"
npm install @innostes/ui lucide-react
```

```bash tab="yarn"
yarn add @innostes/ui lucide-react
```

```bash tab="bun"
bun add @innostes/ui lucide-react
```

</Step>
<Step>

### Configure Tailwind CSS or static styles

Choose the style pipeline that matches your Vite project configuration:

<Tabs items={['Tailwind CSS v4 (Vite plugin)', 'Standard CSS (Without Tailwind)']}>
<Tab value="Tailwind CSS v4 (Vite plugin)">

Install `@tailwindcss/vite` and configure `vite.config.ts`:

```bash
pnpm add -D @tailwindcss/vite tailwindcss
```

```ts title="vite.config.ts"
import { defineConfig } from 'vite';
import react from '@vitejs/plugin-react';
import tailwindcss from '@tailwindcss/vite';

export default defineConfig({
  plugins: [react(), tailwindcss()],
});
```

Then import Tailwind and `@innostes/ui` tokens in `src/index.css`:

```css title="src/index.css"
@import "tailwindcss";
@import "@innostes/ui/tailwind.css";
@import "@innostes/ui/dark.css";
```

</Tab>
<Tab value="Standard CSS (Without Tailwind)">

If your project does not use Tailwind CSS, import the standalone compiled stylesheet in `src/main.tsx`:

```tsx title="src/main.tsx"
import '@innostes/ui/styles.css';
import '@innostes/ui/dark.css';
```

This imports all token variables and component utility classes without injecting a global CSS reset.

</Tab>
</Tabs>

</Step>
<Step>

### Mount root providers

In `src/main.tsx`, wrap the application in `TooltipProvider` and register `Toaster`:

```tsx title="src/main.tsx"
import React from 'react';
import ReactDOM from 'react-dom/client';
import App from './App';
import { TooltipProvider, Toaster, DirectionProvider } from '@innostes/ui';
import './index.css';

ReactDOM.createRoot(document.getElementById('root')!).render(
  <React.StrictMode>
    <DirectionProvider direction="ltr">
      <TooltipProvider delayDuration={200}>
        <App />
        <Toaster position="bottom-end" />
      </TooltipProvider>
    </DirectionProvider>
  </React.StrictMode>,
);
```

</Step>
<Step>

### Create a theme switcher helper

In a Single Page Application without a framework router, toggle dark mode by manipulating the `dark` class on `document.documentElement`:

```tsx title="src/lib/theme.ts"
export function toggleDarkMode() {
  const isDark = document.documentElement.classList.toggle('dark');
  localStorage.setItem('theme', isDark ? 'dark' : 'light');
  return isDark;
}

export function initTheme() {
  const saved = localStorage.getItem('theme');
  const prefersDark = window.matchMedia('(prefers-color-scheme: dark)').matches;
  if (saved === 'dark' || (!saved && prefersDark)) {
    document.documentElement.classList.add('dark');
  } else {
    document.documentElement.classList.remove('dark');
  }
}
```

</Step>
<Step>

### Build your application view

Compose components in `src/App.tsx`:

```tsx title="src/App.tsx"
import React, { useEffect, useState } from 'react';
import { Button, toast } from '@innostes/ui';
import { toggleDarkMode, initTheme } from './lib/theme';
import { Moon, Sun, ShoppingCart } from 'lucide-react';

export default function App() {
  const [isDark, setIsDark] = useState(false);

  useEffect(() => {
    initTheme();
    setIsDark(document.documentElement.classList.contains('dark'));
  }, []);

  const handleToggle = () => {
    const next = toggleDarkMode();
    setIsDark(next);
  };

  return (
    <div className="min-h-screen bg-background text-foreground p-8">
      <div className="max-w-3xl mx-auto space-y-6">
        <header className="flex items-center justify-between border-b border-border pb-4">
          <div>
            <h1 className="text-xl font-bold">Northwind Traders • Dispatch Station</h1>
            <p className="text-xs text-muted-foreground">Whitefield Depot, Bengaluru</p>
          </div>
          <Button variant="outline" size="sm" onClick={handleToggle}>
            {isDark ? <Sun className="size-4 me-1.5" /> : <Moon className="size-4 me-1.5" />}
            {isDark ? 'Light mode' : 'Dark mode'}
          </Button>
        </header>

        <main className="rounded-xl border border-border bg-card p-6 space-y-4">
          <h2 className="text-sm font-semibold">Dispatch Consignment #DISP-9021</h2>
          <p className="text-xs text-muted-foreground">
            3 items packed and ready for carrier collection by Blue Dart Express.
          </p>
          <div className="pt-2">
            <Button
              variant="primary"
              onClick={() => toast.success('Consignment DISP-9021 dispatched')}
            >
              <ShoppingCart className="size-4 me-1.5" />
              Confirm dispatch
            </Button>
          </div>
        </main>
      </div>
    </div>
  );
}
```

</Step>
</Steps>

## Introduction (https://innostes.com/ui/docs)

Enterprise UI component library for ERP and operations systems, built on Base UI and Tailwind CSS.

import { Accessibility, Palette, Terminal, Layers, ShieldCheck, CheckCircle2 } from 'lucide-react';
import { HeroDemo } from '@/components/docs/hero-demo';
import { ComponentIndex } from '@/components/docs/component-index';

`@innostes/ui` is an enterprise component library engineered specifically for back-office applications, enterprise resource planning (ERP) consoles, and high-density operations dashboards.

Designed to meet the demands of operations teams such as Northwind Traders Pvt Ltd, the library provides keyboard-first interaction models, strict type safety, predictable state composition, and full token-based styling.

<HeroDemo />

## Core guarantees

Every component in `@innostes/ui` is governed by explicit architectural policies verified through automated regression suites:

<Cards>
  <Card icon={<Accessibility />} title="WCAG 2.2 AA Conformance" href="/ui/docs/accessibility">
    All interactive primitives satisfy WCAG 2.2 Level AA requirements, including 4.5:1 text contrast, visible keyboard focus indicators, and screen-reader announcements.
  </Card>
  <Card icon={<Layers />} title="React 17, 18, and 19 Support" href="/ui/docs/resources/versioning">
    Tested continuously across React 17.0.2, React 18.3.1, and React 19.0.0 without legacy lifecycle warnings or runtime hook incompatibilities.
  </Card>
  <Card icon={<ShieldCheck />} title="Strict Semantic Versioning" href="/ui/docs/resources/versioning">
    Zero breaking API changes within a major release. Deprecations provide at least one full minor cycle warning with migration pathways.
  </Card>
  <Card icon={<Terminal />} title="Permissive MIT Licence" href="/ui/docs/resources/faq">
    Distributed under the MIT licence for unrestricted commercial use across internal enterprise tools and customer-facing portals.
  </Card>
</Cards>

## Architectural foundation

`@innostes/ui` combines unstyled accessible primitives with token-driven design:

- **Base UI primitives**: Dropdowns, dialogs, popovers, and form fields rely on Base UI for focus trapping, keyboard navigation, and ARIA state management.
- **Tailwind CSS design tokens**: Every colour, spacing increment, and typography rule maps to semantic CSS custom properties defined in OKLCH colour space.
- **Render prop composition**: Clean component substitution using the `render` prop pattern without invalid DOM nesting or ref-forwarding errors.
- **Zero runtime CSS injection**: Styles compile ahead of time through PostCSS and Tailwind, eliminating hydration mismatches and runtime CSS-in-JS overhead.

## Package entry points

The library is organised into four distinct entry points to keep application bundles minimal:

```
@innostes/ui          -> Core UI primitives, forms, data display, and overlays
@innostes/ui/widgets  -> Administrative cards, kanban boards, and audit feeds
@innostes/ui/charts   -> Data visualisation components (requires Recharts)
@innostes/ui/editor   -> Rich text document editing (requires Tiptap)
```

| Entry point | Typical use cases | Peer dependencies |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `@innostes/ui` | Buttons, tables, modals, form inputs, navigation layouts | React, React DOM, Lucide React |
| `@innostes/ui/widgets` | `MetricCard`, `KanbanBoard`, `PermissionMatrix`, `ChangeLog` | None beyond `@innostes/ui` |
| `@innostes/ui/charts` | `CartesianCharts` (bar, line, area), `DonutChart` | `recharts` (>= 2.12.0) |
| `@innostes/ui/editor` | `RichTextEditor`, formatting toolbars, document authoring | `@tiptap/react`, `@tiptap/pm` |

The table below is generated directly from source frontmatter and tracks current stability tiers across all categories:

## Installation (https://innostes.com/ui/docs/installation)

Install @innostes/ui, configure stylesheets, set up providers, and verify your build.

## Requirements

Ensure your environment satisfies the following baseline peer dependencies before installing `@innostes/ui`:

| Dependency | Required version | Verification command |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `react` | `^17.0.0 \|\| ^18.0.0 \|\| ^19.0.0` | `node -p "require('react/package.json').version"` |
| `react-dom` | `^17.0.0 \|\| ^18.0.0 \|\| ^19.0.0` | `node -p "require('react-dom/package.json').version"` |
| `tailwindcss` | `^4.0.0` (recommended) or `^3.4.0` | `npx tailwindcss --version` |

The core primitives from `@base-ui/react`, alongside `clsx`, `tailwind-merge`, and `class-variance-authority`, are bundled with the package and do not require separate installation.

<Steps>
<Step>

### Install the package

Install `@innostes/ui` using your preferred package manager:

```bash tab="pnpm"
pnpm add @innostes/ui
```

```bash tab="npm"
npm install @innostes/ui
```

```bash tab="yarn"
yarn add @innostes/ui
```

```bash tab="bun"
bun add @innostes/ui
```

</Step>
<Step>

### Configure optional peer dependencies

If your application consumes the charts or rich text editor entry points, install the respective peer packages:

<Tabs items={['Charts (@innostes/ui/charts)', 'Editor (@innostes/ui/editor)']}>
<Tab value="Charts (@innostes/ui/charts)">

The charts entry point is built upon `recharts`. Install `recharts` version 2.12.0 or higher:

```bash tab="pnpm"
pnpm add recharts@^2.12.0
```

```bash tab="npm"
npm install recharts@^2.12.0
```

```bash tab="yarn"
yarn add recharts@^2.12.0
```

```bash tab="bun"
bun add recharts@^2.12.0
```

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **React 17 guidance for Recharts**: `recharts` v2 declares `react: "^16.0.0 || ^17.0.0 || ^18.0.0"`. When working in a React 17 environment with npm 7+, strict peer dependency resolution may flag secondary transitive packages. If you encounter an `ERESOLVE unable to resolve dependency tree` warning, install with `--legacy-peer-deps` or add an override to your `package.json`:
>
> ```json title="package.json"
> {
>   "pnpm": {
>     "overrides": {
>       "recharts": "^2.12.0"
>     }
>   }
> }
> ```

</Tab>
<Tab value="Editor (@innostes/ui/editor)">

The rich text editor is built upon Tiptap. Install the core editor dependencies:

```bash tab="pnpm"
pnpm add @tiptap/react @tiptap/pm @tiptap/starter-kit
```

```bash tab="npm"
npm install @tiptap/react @tiptap/pm @tiptap/starter-kit
```

```bash tab="yarn"
yarn add @tiptap/react @tiptap/pm @tiptap/starter-kit
```

```bash tab="bun"
bun add @tiptap/react @tiptap/pm @tiptap/starter-kit
```

</Tab>
</Tabs>

</Step>
<Step>

### Import stylesheets

Configure the design token layers in your application styling pipeline. Choose the approach matching your build setup:

<Tabs items={['Tailwind CSS v4', 'Tailwind CSS v3', 'Without Tailwind CSS']}>
<Tab value="Tailwind CSS v4">

Import the `@innostes/ui` token layers directly after your `@import "tailwindcss";` directive:

```css title="app/global.css"
@import "tailwindcss";
@import "@innostes/ui/tailwind.css";
@import "@innostes/ui/dark.css"; /* Optional dark theme support */
```

Because `@innostes/ui/tailwind.css` declares token defaults via `@theme default`, any custom tokens defined in your project's `@theme` block will take precedence.

</Tab>
<Tab value="Tailwind CSS v3">

Add the `@innostes/ui` compiled distribution files to the Tailwind `content` array so utility classes are not purged:

```js title="tailwind.config.js"
/** @type {import('tailwindcss').Config} */
module.exports = {
  content: [
    './src/**/*.{js,ts,jsx,tsx}',
    './node_modules/@innostes/ui/dist/**/*.{js,mjs}'
  ],
  darkMode: ['class', '[data-theme="dark"]'],
  plugins: []
};
```

Then import the precompiled stylesheet in your CSS entry point:

```css title="src/index.css"
@tailwind base;
@tailwind components;
@tailwind utilities;
@import "@innostes/ui/styles.css";
@import "@innostes/ui/dark.css";
```

</Tab>
<Tab value="Without Tailwind CSS">

For non-Tailwind applications (such as vanilla Vite or Create React App setups), import the standalone compiled stylesheet:

```tsx title="src/main.tsx"
import React from 'react';
import ReactDOM from 'react-dom/client';
import App from './App';
import '@innostes/ui/styles.css';
import '@innostes/ui/dark.css'; // Optional dark theme

ReactDOM.createRoot(document.getElementById('root')!).render(<App />);
```

This standalone stylesheet contains all component utilities and OKLCH variable definitions without resetting global typography or breaking foreign styles.

</Tab>
</Tabs>

</Step>
<Step>

### Mount root providers

Add `Toaster` for global notification management and `TooltipProvider` for shared tooltip delay coordination. If your application supports Right-to-Left (RTL) scripts such as Arabic or Hebrew, wrap the tree in `DirectionProvider`:

```tsx title="app/layout.tsx"
import { Toaster, TooltipProvider, DirectionProvider } from '@innostes/ui';

export default function RootLayout({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) {
  return (
    <html lang="en" suppressHydrationWarning>
      <body>
        <DirectionProvider direction="ltr">
          <TooltipProvider delayDuration={300}>
            {children}
            <Toaster position="bottom-end" />
          </TooltipProvider>
        </DirectionProvider>
      </body>
    </html>
  );
}
```

</Step>
<Step>

### Verify the installation

Confirm your setup by rendering a test component. Create a minimal view with an interactive button:

```tsx title="src/App.tsx"
import { Button, toast } from '@innostes/ui';

export default function App() {
  return (
    <div className="p-8 space-y-4">
      <h1 className="text-xl font-semibold">Northwind Traders Portal</h1>
      <Button
        variant="primary"
        onClick={() => toast.success('Purchase order PO-2026-0881 approved')}
      >
        Approve purchase order
      </Button>
    </div>
  );
}
```

**You should see**: A styled blue button with focus rings on keyboard tab navigation. Clicking the button emits a toast notification at the bottom-end corner of your viewport.

</Step>
</Steps>

## Troubleshooting common issues

### Duplicate React instances

If you encounter errors such as `Invalid hook call` or `Cannot read properties of null (reading 'useMemo')`, your package manager may have installed duplicate copies of `react` or `react-dom`.

**Resolution**: Enforce single-instance resolution in your root `package.json`:

```json title="package.json"
{
  "pnpm": {
    "overrides": {
      "react": "$react",
      "react-dom": "$react-dom"
    }
  }
}
```

For npm, use the `overrides` field; for Yarn, use `resolutions`.

### Component styles not applied

If components render with unstyled default browser inputs or raw HTML buttons:

1. Verify that `@import "@innostes/ui/tailwind.css";` or `@import "@innostes/ui/styles.css";` is present in your global stylesheet.
2. In Tailwind v3, confirm that `'./node_modules/@innostes/ui/dist/**/*.{js,mjs}'` is included in your `tailwind.config.js` `content` glob list.
3. Ensure the CSS import occurs after `@import "tailwindcss";` so that semantic CSS variables override default values.

### Popups rendering behind layout elements

Dropdowns, tooltips, dialogs, and sheets render via a Base UI Portal mounted at `document.body`. If an ancestor element in your DOM tree defines a custom CSS stacking context (`transform`, `filter`, `perspective`, or `opacity < 1`), popups may appear beneath surrounding UI layers.

**Resolution**: Add `isolation: isolate` to the ancestor element, or avoid `overflow: hidden` on parent containers enclosing portal targets.

### SSR hydration warnings

When using dark mode attributes (`class="dark"` or `data-theme="dark"`), browser extensions or pre-render scripts modifying the `<html>` element can trigger React hydration warnings.

**Resolution**: Add `suppressHydrationWarning` to your `<html>` opening tag in `app/layout.tsx`:

```tsx
<html lang="en" suppressHydrationWarning>
```

This prevents React from reporting mismatches when theme attributes are populated before JavaScript execution.

## Application shell (https://innostes.com/ui/docs/patterns/app-shell)

Composable layout scaffolding for multi-tenant enterprise dashboards.

# Application shell

The application shell provides the structural frame within which ERP modules operate. Comprising `AppRail`, `Sidebar`, `TopBar`, and `PageHeader`, it maintains continuous context, breadcrumb paths, and user account actions.

## Structure

1. **Primary rail**: High-level module switching (Procurement, Inventory, Finance, Human Resources).
2. **Context sidebar**: Deep navigational trees, collapsible folders, and saved view bookmarks.
3. **Top bar**: Global command palette trigger, notification bell, and user profile switcher.
4. **Canvas**: Main content region with dynamic page headers and breadcrumbs.

## Complex forms (https://innostes.com/ui/docs/patterns/complex-forms)

Architecture for multi-section data entry, validation, and unsaved changes.

# Complex forms

Enterprise procurement, invoicing, and inventory intake require structured data collection spanning dozens of interrelated fields. The complex forms pattern orchestrates `FormLayout`, `Field`, input groups, and validation feedback into a coherent operator experience.

## Design principles

- **Sectional grouping**: Divide extensive forms into logical cards or accordion steps to reduce visual fatigue.
- **Immediate validation**: Validate fields on blur and on submit, displaying inline errors via `FieldError` linked with `aria-describedby`.
- **Dirty state protection**: Track form dirty state and warn operators before navigating away from incomplete transactions.

---

## Data management (https://innostes.com/ui/docs/patterns/data-management)

Patterns for enterprise data tables, batch actions, and filtering.

# Data management

High-volume operations at Northwind Traders Pvt Ltd involve browsing, filtering, and updating thousands of shipment records and customer accounts. The data management pattern defines how `DataTable`, `Pagination`, search bars, and batch action toolbars collaborate.

## Key considerations

- **Server-driven state**: Sorting, pagination, and multi-field filtering query the backend directly, preserving URL search parameters for link sharing.
- **Batch execution**: Selection toolbars appear upon selecting records, allowing bulk state transitions (e.g. "Approve selected", "Export to CSV").
- **Responsive fallback**: On narrow mobile viewports, tables adapt into card lists or horizontally scrollable containers with pinned identity columns.

## Patterns (https://innostes.com/ui/docs/patterns/index)

Reusable composition recipes for enterprise application architectures.

# Patterns

Patterns document established combinations of primitives and widgets that resolve recurrent enterprise challenges at Northwind Traders Pvt Ltd. Rather than prescribing rigid page templates, patterns offer composable blueprints for forms, data tables, and application shells.

## Core patterns

- **Complex forms**: Multi-section data entry, conditional validation with Zod, unsaved changes detection, and accessible error summaries.
- **Data management**: High-density server tables, compound filtering drawers, batch selection workflows, and export pipelines.
- **Application shell**: Responsive dual-tier navigation, persistent command bars, collapsible sidebars, and contextual breadcrumbs.

Development guidelines, code standards, and PR submission workflows.

# Contributing

Contributions to `@innostes/ui` are welcome from engineering teams across Northwind Traders Pvt Ltd. This guide outlines local environment setup, testing requirements, and quality checks required before submitting pull requests.

## Workflow

1. **Monorepo setup**: Clone the repository and install dependencies with `pnpm install`.
2. **Component development**: Implement new primitives in `packages/ui/src/` adhering strictly to Base UI conventions and British English TSDoc.
3. **Automated verification**: Run uncached quality gates before raising a pull request:
   ```bash
   pnpm nx run-many -t test typecheck build -p ui --skip-nx-cache
   pnpm nx run landing:docs-check
   ```
4. **Documentation**: Every new component requires complete documentation adhering to the component template.

## API Conventions (https://innostes.com/ui/docs/resources/conventions)

Core architectural principles, state models, polymorphic composition, and styling conventions across @innostes/ui.

`@innostes/ui` adheres to strict architectural conventions across all primitives. Learning these conventions allows developers to predict prop names, event payloads, composition patterns, and styling hooks across the entire design system.

## Composition & exports

All components are exported as flat, named exports from the package entry points. Primitives with multiple child slots (such as `Dialog`, `Select`, or `Tabs`) are imported individually rather than accessed via namespaces:

```tsx
import { Dialog, DialogTrigger, DialogContent, DialogTitle } from '@innostes/ui';
import { MetricCard } from '@innostes/ui/widgets';
import { CartesianCharts } from '@innostes/ui/charts';
```

All exports are fully tree-shakeable: your bundler includes only the code for components your application imports.

## Controlled & uncontrolled state

Every stateful primitive supports both uncontrolled and controlled operation using standard React naming conventions:

| Uncontrolled prop | Controlled prop | Change callback | Event details payload |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `defaultValue` | `value` | `onValueChange(value, eventDetails)` | `{ reason?: string; event: Event }` |
| `defaultOpen` | `open` | `onOpenChange(open, eventDetails)` | `{ reason?: string; event: Event }` |
| `defaultChecked` | `checked` | `onCheckedChange(checked, eventDetails)` | `{ event: Event }` |
| `defaultPressed` | `pressed` | `onPressedChange(pressed, eventDetails)` | `{ event: Event }` |

### Event details pattern

Callbacks pass the updated value as the first argument, followed by an optional `eventDetails` object indicating the origin trigger (e.g. keyboard escape vs pointer click):

```tsx
<Dialog
  open={isOpen}
  onOpenChange={(nextOpen, details) => {
    if (!nextOpen && details?.reason === 'outside-press') {
      // Prevent closing when user clicks outside modal
      return;
    }
    setIsOpen(nextOpen);
  }}
>
  {/* Modal contents */}
</Dialog>
```

## Polymorphism with the `render` prop

`@innostes/ui` avoids the legacy Radix `asChild` pattern. Instead, primitives built on Base UI utilize the **`render` prop** pattern. This merges accessibility attributes, focus handlers, and class names directly into the custom child element:

```tsx
import Link from 'next/link';
import { Button } from '@innostes/ui';

// Compose an accessible button that renders as a Next.js client link
<Button
  variant="primary"
  nativeButton={false}
  render={<Link href="/orders/PO-2026-0881" />}
>
  View purchase order
</Button>
```

When delegating button rendering to a link element (`<a>`), specify `nativeButton={false}` so the component does not emit an invalid HTML `<button>` inside an anchor.

## Customisation

`@innostes/ui` provides four distinct layers for styling overrides:

### 1. The `className` prop

The `className` prop applies to the component root. Passed classes are merged through `tailwind-merge`, ensuring that user-provided utilities override internal defaults:

```tsx
<Button className="w-full justify-start font-mono">
  PO-2026-0881
</Button>
```

On interactive primitives, `className` can also accept a function receiving the current component state:

```tsx
<Button className={({ disabled }) => (disabled ? 'opacity-40 cursor-not-allowed' : '')}>
  Submit order
</Button>
```

### 2. Multi-part styling with `classNames`

Composite widgets and complex data display components provide a `classNames` prop accepting a map of slot names to utility strings:

```tsx
<MetricCard
  label="Total Procurement"
  value="₹1,45,280.00"
  classNames={{
    root: 'border-blue-500/30 bg-blue-50/10',
    label: 'text-blue-700 dark:text-blue-400 font-semibold',
    value: 'font-mono text-2xl tracking-tight',
  }}
/>
```

### 3. The `data-slot` attribute

Every internal element emits a deterministic `data-slot` attribute (e.g. `data-slot="dialog-content"`, `data-slot="card-header"`). You can target child slots from parent stylesheets or container selectors:

```css
/* Customise all metric card values inside a financial summary section */
.finance-overview [data-slot="metric-card-value"] {
  font-family: var(--font-mono);
  color: var(--color-emerald-700);
}
```

### 4. Interactive state attributes

Primitives expose interactive state via HTML `data-*` attributes (`data-state="open"`, `data-checked`, `data-disabled`, `data-highlighted`, `data-invalid`). You can style these states using Tailwind CSS variants:

```tsx
<div className="border-border data-invalid:border-destructive data-invalid:ring-destructive">
  {/* Field contents */}
</div>
```

### 5. Server-safe variant helpers

Every styled component exports its underlying class-variance-authority helper function (e.g. `buttonVariants()`, `badgeVariants()`, `inputVariants()`). These functions are pure JavaScript and execute safely on the server:

```tsx
import { buttonVariants } from '@innostes/ui';

// Generate button styles for standard HTML or external router links
const linkClasses = buttonVariants({ variant: 'outline', size: 'sm' });
```

## Ref forwarding

Every component wraps its DOM root in React's `forwardRef`. Refs point directly to native DOM elements (`HTMLButtonElement`, `HTMLDivElement`, `HTMLInputElement`), allowing direct integration with form management libraries (such as React Hook Form) across React 17, React 18, and React 19.

## Server Components & client boundaries

- **Interactive components** declare `'use client'` at their file headers. You can import them directly into Server Components in Next.js App Router without manual wrappers.
- **Pure helpers** (`cn()`, `formatDate()`, `buttonVariants()`, `badgeVariants()`) do not import browser-specific APIs and execute on both client and server.

## Standard size scale

Interactive controls share a unified size scale so adjacent controls align in toolbars and data tables:

| Size | Height | Recommended application |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `sm` | 32px | High-density audit grids, compact filter bars, table pagination |
| `md` | 40px | Standard forms, default modal actions, primary toolbars |
| `lg` | 48px | Mobile ERP terminals, high-consequence confirmation dialogs |

## Internationalisation & RTL support

All customer-facing text is customizable to support enterprise multi-language requirements. Rather than hardcoding English strings, components expose override props:

- `closeLabel`: Dialog, Alert, Sheet dismissal labels (defaults to `"Close"`).
- `labels`: Component-specific string maps (e.g. `labels={{ previousPage: 'Previous', nextPage: 'Next' }}` on `Pagination`).
- **Logical CSS properties**: Styles use CSS logical properties (`margin-inline-end`, `inset-inline-start`, `border-inline-start`) instead of physical directions (`left`, `right`, `mr-`, `ml-`). Wrap the application in `<DirectionProvider direction="rtl">` for Arabic, Hebrew, or Urdu localization.

---

## FAQ (https://innostes.com/ui/docs/resources/faq)

Frequently asked questions regarding @innostes/ui installation, theming, and usage.

# Frequently asked questions

Common questions and answers regarding `@innostes/ui` integration and enterprise usage.

## General

### How does innostes UI differ from standard Tailwind component libraries?

`@innostes/ui` is built directly on Base UI unstyled primitives, ensuring full WAI-ARIA compliance, roving focus management, and keyboard accessibility by default. Tailwind CSS v4 provides token-based styling rather than arbitrary utility classes.

### Can I use innostes UI with React 17 or React 18?

Yes. The package is thoroughly tested and verified across React 17, React 18, and React 19 runtimes using dedicated test matrices in our CI pipeline.

### Does the library support dark mode?

Yes. All components consume OKLCH semantic variables that dynamically adjust when toggling between `.light` and `.dark` class names or `data-theme` attributes on the root container.
